summary: Tier-10 plan for EDC.7–8 with the Weil-weight prerequisite closure owned locally, perverse purity/decomposition/relative hard Lefschetz and scheme correspondence traces. The 65 higher-tier weight provenance targets are represented by 57 target-level nodes, absorbing small steps and importing the existing scheme Frobenius. The singular semisimple isolated-point theorem uses the full Artin fixed subscheme and a finite-jet character argument, independent of the false reduced-point cone claims. Native categorical and Frobenius linear-algebra statements remain compact. Both stages are planned; implementation, exact supplier augmentations and separate Part II scopes remain open for independent review.

conventions: Weights are owned by the EDC.7 weight foundations below: integer Weil weights and fixed-ι real weights are distinct. K has weights ≤w when ℋ^iK has punctual weights ≤w+i; ≥w means DK≤−w. Geometric Frobenius on ℚ̄_ℓ(1) is q⁻¹, so Tate twist r subtracts 2r; shifting by m adds m.
Perverse normalisation: IC_X(L) = j_!*(L[d]) with no Tate half-twist; L lisse punctually pure of weight w gives IC of weight w + d.
Coefficients: ℚ̄_ℓ as the 2-colimit over finite E/ℚ_ℓ of the rational adic categories of EDC.6; finite-field arithmetic objects carry an index 0 (X₀, F₀), their pullbacks to 𝔽̄_q drop it.

Cohomological correspondences: u : c₁^*F₁ → c₂^!F₂ (pull back along the first leg); the graph-type correspondence of g is (g, id), whose c-morphisms are u : g^*F → F; the n-th Frobenius twist is (Fr^n ∘ c₁, c₂).
Duality data for the functional equation: Δ := ∏_i det(F_i)^{(−1)^i}, so Δ² = q^{dχ}, the convention of WeilConjectures:WC.2.

nodes.title: Perverse sheaves over 𝔽_q as Frobenius-equivariant perverse sheaves over 𝔽̄_q
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be separated of finite type over 𝔽_q and K₀, L₀ ∈ D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ), with pullbacks K, L to X. (a) For every i there is a short exact sequence 0 → Hom^{i−1}(K, L)_F → Hom^i(K₀, L₀) → Hom^i(K, L)^F → 0, where Hom^i := Hom(−, −[i]) in the derived category, F is the geometric Frobenius acting on the finite-dimensional ℚ̄_ℓ-space Hom^i(K, L) = H^i RHom(K, L) by transport of structure, and the subscript/superscript F denote coinvariants/invariants. (b) The functor sending a perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ to the pair (F, φ), φ : Fr*F ≅ F its Weil descent isomorphism, is fully faithful from Perv(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) to the category of perverse sheaves on X equipped with an isomorphism Fr*F ≅ F, and its essential image is stable under extensions and under subquotients. (c) The functor is not essentially surjective: over X₀ = Spec 𝔽_q the pair (ℚ̄_ℓ, multiplication by a non-unit u ∈ ℚ̄_ℓ^×) is not in the image.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
The Frobenius acting on Hom^i(K, L) is the one induced by the descent data of K₀ and L₀; continuous Galois cohomology of Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂ is used.
proofSteps: Apply the requested adic Hochschild–Serre comparison to RΓ(X₀, RHom(K₀,L₀)). Its geometric coefficient complex is RHom_X(K,L) with the action induced by the two descent data. This is Galois descent, and requires no proper or smooth structural morphism. The finite/discrete supplier theorem alone does not supply this adic comparison.

The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂ has only the columns p = 0, 1, since continuous cohomology of ℤ̂ with finite-dimensional ℓ-adic coefficients is invariants in degree 0, coinvariants in degree 1 and zero above; this gives (a) (BBD (5.1.2.3)–(5.1.2.5)).
For perverse K₀, L₀ the group Hom^{−1}(K, L) vanishes (EDC.5/heart-abelian-subcategory), so (a) with i = 0 gives full faithfulness: Hom(K₀, L₀) = Hom(K, L)^F.

With i = 1, Ext¹ in Perv(X₀) and Ext¹ in the category of pairs (F, φ) both sit in exact sequences with Hom(K, L)_F on the left and Ext¹(K, L)^F on the right; equal dimensions and injectivity give a bijection, hence stability under extensions.

Stability under subquotients follows from the noetherian-induction Lemma 5.1.3 of BBD: on a smooth dense open where a sub-object is a shifted lisse sheaf, a Frobenius-stable lisse subquotient descends; extend by p j_!, p j_* and the closed complement.
The non-example over a point: a Weil-descent isomorphism of ℚ̄_ℓ which is multiplication by a non-ℓ-adic unit is not the Frobenius of a continuous ℓ-adic Galois representation.
acceptance: Over X₀ = Spec 𝔽_q, K₀ = L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ: Hom^0 = ℚ̄_ℓ and Hom^1(K₀, L₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ (coinvariants of the trivial action), while Hom^1(K, L) = 0.
For K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ and L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ(1) on Spec 𝔽_q: F acts on Hom(K, L) = ℚ̄_ℓ by q^{-1} ≠ 1, so invariants and coinvariants vanish and Hom^i(K₀, L₀) = 0 for all i.

sources.match: BBD prove full faithfulness of the extension-of-scalars functor on perverse sheaves with its Frobenius isomorphism, stability of the essential image under extensions and subquotients, the short exact sequences (5.1.2.5) for Hom^i, and give the non-unit counterexample over a point.

nodes.title: Mixed perverse sheaves and the perverse t-structure on mixed complexes
nodes.statement: For X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q, let D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) ⊂ D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) be the full triangulated subcategory of mixed complexes (EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes). The middle perverse t-structure of D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) restricts to a t-structure on D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ); its heart Perv_m(X₀) is the category of mixed perverse sheaves: perverse sheaves on X₀ whose ordinary cohomology sheaves are mixed. Perv_m(X₀) is a full abelian subcategory of Perv(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) stable under kernels, cokernels, extensions and all subquotients. A mixed perverse sheaf F₀ has weights ≤ w (resp. ≥ w, pure of weight w) when F₀ ∈ D^b_m has; with the shifted convention of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes, F₀[1] has weights ≤ w + 1 exactly when F₀ has weights ≤ w.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Mixedness is tested on ordinary cohomology sheaves; perverse truncations are computed in D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ).
proofSteps: D^b_m(X₀) is stable under f^*, Rf_*, Rf_!, Rf^!, ⊗, RHom and Verdier duality (EDC.7/weight-six-operations-preserve-mixedness-6-1-11) and under the ordinary truncations, since mixedness is a condition on cohomology sheaves (BBD 5.1.6).

The perverse truncations are built from these operations along a stratification (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure, gluing), so they preserve D^b_m; hence the perverse t-structure restricts (BBD 5.1.7(i)).
The heart of the restricted t-structure is a full subcategory of Perv(X₀) stable under kernels, cokernels and extensions (it is the intersection with a triangulated subcategory).

Stability under subquotients: apply BBD Lemma 5.1.3/Remark 5.1.4 to the system of subcategories Perv_m(Y₀) for all subschemes Y₀, whose hypotheses (stability under p j_!, p j_*, closed pushforward, lisse subquotients on smooth strata) hold by EDC.7/weight-six-operations-preserve-mixedness-6-1-11 (BBD 5.1.7(ii)).
acceptance: ℚ̄_ℓ[d] on a smooth pure d-dimensional X₀ is mixed perverse and pure of weight d.
On Spec 𝔽_q, Perv_m is the category of finite-dimensional continuous ℚ̄_ℓ-representations of Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) whose Frobenius eigenvalues are q-Weil numbers of integer weight.

uses.how: the weight filtration and the perverse-cohomology weight criterion live in Perv_m(X₀)

sources.match: BBD recall punctual purity and mixedness, define D^b_m by mixed cohomology sheaves, prove that the perverse t-structure induces one on D^b_m and that subquotients of mixed perverse sheaves are mixed (Stabilités 5.1.7), and define weights ≤ w, ≥ w and purity with the shift in i (5.1.8).
Stability of mixed complexes under the operations and the definition of complexes of weights ≤ w, ≥ w.

nodes.title: Weights are tested at closed points and are insensitive to finite extension of 𝔽_q
nodes.statement: Let K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ). (a) K₀ has weights ≤ w iff i_x^*K₀ has weights ≤ w for every closed point x of X₀; it has weights ≥ w iff i_x^!K₀ has weights ≥ w for every closed point x. (b) For n ≥ 1 the pullback of a specified arithmetic K₀ to X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{qⁿ} is mixed, or has either weight bound, iff K₀ does. This compares compatible arithmetic descents: a bare geometric object can have different weights under different Frobenius descents. (c) For nonzero mixed complexes K₀,L₀ the optimal upper weight of K₀ ⊠ L₀ is the sum of their optimal upper weights, and its optimal lower weight is the sum of their optimal lower weights. For arbitrary complexes the inequalities remain valid, including the zero object; the displayed equalities are asserted only for nonzero factors.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
In (c), X₀ × Y₀ is the fibre product over 𝔽_q and K₀ ⊠ L₀ := pr₁^*K₀ ⊗ pr₂^*L₀.
proofSteps: (a), first half: weights ≤ w are defined by the punctual weights of ℋ^i, i.e. by the stalks at closed points, which are the cohomology of i_x^*K₀.
(a), second half: K₀ has weights ≥ w iff D K₀ has weights ≤ −w; apply the first half to D K₀ and use i_x^* D = D i_x^! (EDC.1:biduality/duality-exchange-isomorphisms).

(b): the closed points of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{qⁿ} lie over those of X₀ and the Frobenius of the residue field of a point over x is a power of that of x; Weil q^{deg}-numbers of weight w are preserved and detected by powers.

(c): the upper bound ≤ w + w′ is stability of ⊗ and pullback (Weight estimates for the six operations (EDC.7 weight foundations)); equality is checked at closed points (a), where the stalk of K₀ ⊠ L₀ at (x, y) is the tensor product of the stalks and eigenvalue weights add; the lower bound follows by duality since ⊠ commutes with Verdier duality (EDC.1:biduality, Künneth for dualizing complexes).
acceptance: ℚ̄_ℓ on 𝔸¹_{𝔽_q} is pure of weight 0: at every closed point x, i_x^*ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0 and i_x^!ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[−2] has weight 2 − 2 = 0; its perverse shift ℚ̄_ℓ[1] is pure of weight 1.
ℚ̄_ℓ(1) ⊠ ℚ̄_ℓ(1) on Spec 𝔽_q is ℚ̄_ℓ(2), of weight −4 = (−2) + (−2).

The geometric rank-one sheaf on a point admits arithmetic descents with Frobenius 1 and q; they have weights 0 and 2 respectively. Finite extension of one chosen descent preserves its weight, but does not identify these descents.

sources.match: BBD test weights ≤ w by i_x^* and ≥ w by i_x^! at closed points, note invariance under finite extension of the finite field, and prove that weights add exactly under external tensor products.

nodes.title: Ext-vanishing between weights
nodes.statement: Let K₀, L₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) and w ∈ ℤ. (a) If K₀ has weights ≤ w and L₀ has weights > w (i.e. ≥ w + 1), then Ra_*RHom(K₀, L₀) ∈ D_{>0}(Spec 𝔽_q) for a : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q, and Hom(K₀, L₀[i]) = 0 for all i > 0. (b) If K₀ has weights ≤ w and L₀ has weights ≥ w, then F has no invariants on Hom(K, L[i]) for i > 0, so the restriction Hom(K₀, L₀[i]) → Hom(K, L[i]) is zero for i > 0, and Hom(K₀, L₀[i]) = 0 for i ≥ 2. (c) In particular, for mixed perverse K₀ of weights ≤ w and L₀ of weights > w: Hom(K₀, L₀) = 0 and Ext¹_{Perv(X₀)}(K₀, L₀) = 0; for simple mixed perverse U₀, V₀ pure of weights u > v, Ext¹(V₀, U₀) = 0.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: RHom(K₀, L₀) has weights ≥ (w+1) − w = 1 by Weight estimates for the six operations (EDC.7 weight foundations) (v), and Ra_* preserves lower bounds (ii); so Ra_*RHom ∈ D_{≥1} = D_{>0}, giving (a) first part (BBD 5.1.15(i)).
On Spec 𝔽_q, a complex of weights > 0 has H^i of weights > i ≥ 0 for i ≥ 0, so Frobenius has no eigenvalue 1: invariants and coinvariants of Hom^i(K, L) vanish for i ≥ 0.
Insert into the exact sequences of EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves: Hom^i(K₀, L₀) = 0 for i > 0, which is (a) (BBD 5.1.15(ii)).
With weights ≥ w for L₀, Hom^i(K, L) has weights ≥ i, hence > 0 for i ≥ 1: invariants vanish for i > 0 and coinvariants vanish for i ≥ 1, giving (b) (BBD 5.1.15(iii)).
(c): for perverse K₀, L₀, Hom^0 = Hom(K, L)^F with weights > 0 has no invariants; Ext¹ in Perv is Hom^1 (EDC.5/heart-abelian-subcategory). The simple pure case is the instance used in BBD 5.3.5.
acceptance: K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ, L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) on Spec 𝔽_q (weights 0 and 2): Hom^i(K₀, L₀) = 0 for all i, since Frobenius acts by q ≠ 1.
Sharpness of the strict inequality: K₀ = L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ on Spec 𝔽_q (both of weight 0) has Ext¹(K₀, L₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ ≠ 0, realised by the unipotent rank-two sheaf E₂.

sources.locator: Proposition 5.1.15 (i)–(iii) and its proof, p. 129 (checked on the page image)
sources.match: BBD: for K₀ of weights ≤ w and L₀ of weights > w, Ra_*RHom is in D_{>0} and Hom^i vanishes for i > 0; for L₀ of weights ≥ w the Frobenius invariants of Hom^i(K, L) vanish for i > 0, so the restriction maps are zero.

nodes.title: Lower weights of a mixed perverse sheaf are detected by H⁰ on affine étale opens
nodes.statement: A mixed perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ has weights ≥ w iff for every affine étale map u : U₀ → X₀ the Frobenius module H⁰(U, u^*F) (hypercohomology of the pullback over 𝔽̄_q, with U₀ defined over a finite extension 𝔽_{qⁿ} as allowed by EDC.7/pointwise-weight-criteria (b)) has weights ≥ w.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
U₀ → X₀ étale with U₀ affine; H⁰ is hypercohomology of the complex u^*F over 𝔽̄_q.
proofSteps: Necessity: u^! = u^* for étale u preserves weights ≥ w, and RΓ = Ra_* preserves lower bounds (Weight estimates for the six operations (EDC.7 weight foundations) (ii)); H⁰ of a complex of weights ≥ w has weights ≥ w.

For curves follow BBD 5.2.2: use the classification of simple perverse constituents, affine étale neighbourhoods with many preimages of a selected point, and the estimates for H⁻¹ and H⁰. Their dimensions force the lower bound on the punctual part and on the lisse constituents.

The higher-dimensional argument is BBD 5.2.3–5.2.8, not a formal restriction-to-curves argument. Choose a finite map to a product of curves and towers of finite étale covers on those curves. The cohomology-growth theorem BBD 4.5.4–4.5.5 bounds negative cohomology by a polynomial of smaller degree than the top growth term. The trace comparison in 5.2.5–5.2.7 excludes a constituent of weight below w; noetherian induction handles the closed complement. The dedicated Betti-growth node lists the nearby-cycle and curve-Euler-characteristic inputs; it is not supplied by the early perverse theorem alone.
The weights of H⁰(U, F) are those of the Frobenius of 𝔽_{qⁿ} acting by transport of structure (BBD 5.1.11–5.1.12).
acceptance: F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on 𝔾_{m,𝔽_q}: H⁰(𝔾_m, ℚ̄_ℓ[1]) = H¹(𝔾_m, ℚ̄_ℓ) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weight 2 ≥ 1, consistent with weights ≥ 1, while H^{−1} = H⁰(𝔾_m) has weight 0 < 1 and is not tested.
A punctual perverse sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ(1) at a rational point has H⁰ = ℚ̄_ℓ(1) of weight −2 on every affine étale neighbourhood, so it does not have weights ≥ −1.

sources.match: BBD characterise lower weights of a mixed perverse sheaf by the weights of H⁰(U, F) on affine étale U, first on smooth curves and then in general.

nodes.title: Subquotients of mixed perverse sheaves keep their weight bounds
nodes.statement: If a mixed perverse sheaf F₀ has weights ≥ w (resp. ≤ w), every subquotient of F₀ in Perv(X₀) has weights ≥ w (resp. ≤ w).
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: For a quotient G₀ of F₀ and affine étale U, Artin vanishing makes H⁰(U,F) → H⁰(U,G) surjective; hence the lower bound ≥ w passes to G by the affine H⁰ criterion.

For a subobject G₀ ⊂ F₀ the exact sequence H⁻¹(U,F/G) → H⁰(U,G) → H⁰(U,F) first gives G₀ weights ≥ w−1. Apply the same argument to G₀ ⊠ G₀ ⊂ F₀ ⊠ F₀: the external product is perverse and exact in each argument by the EDC.5 request, and F₀ ⊠ F₀ has weights ≥ 2w. Thus 2·(the optimal lower weight of G₀) ≥ 2w−1, which gives ≥ w by integrality. Treat G₀=0 separately. This avoids using a nonexistent integral Tate half-twist when w is odd.
Verdier duality exchanges subobjects and quotients and reverses weights, giving the upper bound ≤ w. This is BBD 5.3.1.
acceptance: On Spec 𝔽_q the unipotent rank-two sheaf E₂ (Frobenius a single Jordan block with eigenvalue 1) is pure of weight 0, and its unique rank-one subobject and quotient ℚ̄_ℓ are pure of weight 0.
On Spec 𝔽_q, ℚ̄_ℓ ⊕ ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weights ≤ 2 and ≥ 0; its quotient ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weight 2 ≤ 2 and its subobject ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0 ≥ 0, while neither bound can be improved for the sum.

sources.match: BBD show that subquotients of a mixed perverse sheaf of weights ≥ w (≤ w) keep the bound, via H⁰ on affines, the external-square trick and integrality of weights, and obtain the upper bound by duality.

nodes.title: Intermediate extension along an affine immersion preserves weights; purity of IC
nodes.statement: (a) Let j : U₀ ↪ X₀ be an affine locally closed immersion and F₀ a mixed perverse sheaf on U₀. If F₀ has weights ≤ w (resp. ≥ w), so does j_!*F₀; if F₀ is pure of weight w, j_!*F₀ is pure of weight w. (b) Let X₀ be irreducible of dimension d, U₀ ⊂ X₀ a dense open subscheme smooth over 𝔽_q and L₀ a lisse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaf on U₀ punctually pure of weight w. Then the intersection complex IC_{X₀}(L₀) = j_!*(L₀[d]) of EDC.5/intersection-complex-of-local-system is a pure perverse sheaf of weight w + d; in particular IC_{X₀} := IC_{X₀}(ℚ̄_ℓ) is pure of weight d. (c) Consequently, for X₀ proper over 𝔽_q, the intersection cohomology H^i(X, IC_X(L)) is pure of weight w + d + i for every i.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
(a): j affine (j_! and Rj_* are then t-exact for the perverse t-structure). (b): the shift is the perverse normalisation L₀[d]; no Tate half-twist is built in.
proofSteps: (a) Since j is affine and quasi-finite, j_!F₀ and Rj_*F₀ are perverse (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing, BBD 4.1.3).

If F₀ has weights ≤ w, j_!F₀ has weights ≤ w (Weight estimates for the six operations (EDC.7 weight foundations) (i)); j_!*F₀ is the image of j_!F₀ → Rj_*F₀, a quotient of j_!F₀ in Perv(X₀), so it has weights ≤ w by EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability.
Dually, if F₀ has weights ≥ w, Rj_*F₀ has weights ≥ w and its subobject j_!*F₀ has weights ≥ w; combining both gives purity (BBD 5.3.2, first proof).

(b) L₀[d] is pure of weight w + d on the smooth U₀ (Purity on a smooth scheme is pointwise purity of lisse cohomology sheaves (EDC.7 weight foundations) (c)) and perverse (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse). Shrink U₀ to an affine dense open (IC is independent of the dense open, EDC.5/intersection-complex-of-local-system); a morphism from an affine scheme to the separated X₀ is affine, so U₀ ↪ X₀ is an affine immersion; apply (a).

(c) Proper pushforward to Spec 𝔽_q preserves purity (Proper direct images of pure complexes are pure (EDC.7 weight foundations)): RΓ(X, IC) is pure of weight w + d, so H^i is pure of weight w + d + i.
acceptance: For a smooth projective curve C₀ and L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ: IC = ℚ̄_ℓ[1], pure of weight 1, and H^i(C, ℚ̄_ℓ[1]) = H^{i+1}(C, ℚ̄_ℓ) is pure of weight i + 1.

For the split nodal cubic X₀ with normalisation ν : ℙ¹ → X₀ (ν finite birational), IC_{X₀} = ν_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1], so IH^0(X) = H¹(ℙ¹) = 0 although H¹(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) = ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0: the constant sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on X₀ is not pure of weight 1.
The specialisation X₀ smooth projective of dimension d gives IC = ℚ̄_ℓ[d] and recovers purity of H^i(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) of weight i (the Weil II weight inputs (EDC.7 weight foundations), Weil II 3.3.9).

sources.locator: Corollaire 5.3.2 with its first proof, p. 135
sources.match: BBD prove that for an affine immersion j the intermediate extension of a mixed perverse sheaf of weights ≤ w (≥ w) keeps the bound, so pure goes to pure of the same weight, via perversity of j_! and the quotient j_!F → j_!*F.
Shifted lisse pure sheaves on smooth schemes are pure, and proper direct images preserve purity.

nodes.title: Simple mixed perverse sheaves are pure
nodes.statement: Every simple object of Perv_m(X₀) is pure: it is isomorphic to i_*j_!*(L₀[d]) for i the closure of a smooth connected locally closed U₀ ⊂ X₀ of dimension d, j : U₀ ↪ Ū₀ open and L₀ an irreducible lisse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaf on U₀ punctually pure of some integer weight β, and it is pure of weight β + d.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: A simple mixed perverse sheaf is simple in Perv(X₀) (EDC.7/mixed-perverse-sheaves: subobjects of mixed are mixed), so it is i_*j_!*(L₀[d]) with L₀ irreducible lisse on a smooth connected U₀ (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification, applied to arithmetic objects through EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves).

Shrink U₀ (allowed, EDC.5/intersection-complex-of-local-system): L₀ is mixed and irreducible, so its weight filtration by lisse subsheaves (EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness; Weil II 3.4.1(ii)) has a single step and L₀ is punctually pure.
Take U₀ affine and apply EDC.7/intersection-complex-purity (BBD 5.3.4).
acceptance: The punctual simple perverse sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ(r) at a closed point is pure of weight −2r.
On Spec 𝔽_q a simple mixed perverse sheaf is a one-dimensional continuous ℚ̄_ℓ-representation whose Frobenius eigenvalue is a q-Weil number of some integer weight β, and it is pure of weight β.

sources.match: BBD: every simple mixed perverse sheaf is pure, by writing it as an intermediate extension of an irreducible, hence pure, lisse sheaf on an affine smooth open.

nodes.title: Splitting lemma for a partition of simple objects with Ext¹-vanishing
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian category in which every object has finite length. Let S⁺ ⊔ S⁻ be a partition of the isomorphism classes of simple objects, and A⁺ (resp. A⁻) the full subcategory of objects all of whose simple subquotients lie in S⁺ (resp. S⁻). Assume every short exact sequence 0 → U → E → V → 0 with U ∈ S⁺ and V ∈ S⁻ splits. Then every object F has a unique subobject W F ∈ A⁻ with F / W F ∈ A⁺; Hom(A⁺, A⁻) = Hom(A⁻, A⁺) = 0 and Ext¹(A⁻, A⁺) = 0; and every morphism f : F → G satisfies f(W F) = f(F) ∩ W G.
hypotheses: A abelian, every object of finite length (artinian and noetherian); the partition is of isomorphism classes of simple objects; Ext¹ vanishing is only required from S⁻ to S⁺.
proofSteps: Ext¹(Y, X) = 0 for X ∈ A⁺, Y ∈ A⁻ by dévissage along composition series and the long exact Ext sequence; Hom vanishings because A⁺ and A⁻ share no simple constituents.

Existence by induction on length: choose a simple subobject S ⊂ F and W(F/S); its preimage E is an extension of W(F/S) by S. If S ∈ S⁻ take W F = E; if S ∈ S⁺ the extension splits by Ext¹(W(F/S), S) = 0, take a lift of W(F/S).
Uniqueness: for two candidates W′, W″ the composites W′ → F → F/W″ and W″ → F → F/W′ vanish by Hom(A⁻, A⁺) = 0.
Strictness: both f(W F) and f(F) ∩ W G have the characteristic property of W(f(F)).
acceptance: A = finite-dimensional representations of ℤ over ℚ̄_ℓ on which the generator acts with eigenvalues in {1, q}, S⁻ = {eigenvalue 1}, S⁺ = {eigenvalue q}: W F is the generalized 1-eigenspace and the splitting is the generalized eigenspace decomposition.

Without the Ext¹ hypothesis the conclusion fails: for finite-dimensional representations of the quiver 1 → 2 over a field, the indecomposable projective P₁ is a non-split extension of S₁ by S₂; with S⁻ = {S₁} and S⁺ = {S₂}, its subobjects are 0, S₂ and P₁, and none lies in A⁻ with quotient in A⁺.

sources.match: BBD's abstract lemma: in a finite-length abelian category with a partition of simples and vanishing Ext¹ from the second class to the first, each object has a unique subobject in A⁻ with quotient in A⁺, functorial and strict.

nodes.title: The weight filtration of a mixed perverse sheaf

planet.name: Weight filtration of mixed perverse sheaves

nodes.statement: Every mixed perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ has a unique finite increasing filtration W = (W_i F₀)_{i ∈ ℤ} by perverse subsheaves, with W_i F₀ = 0 for i ≪ 0 and W_i F₀ = F₀ for i ≫ 0, such that Gr^W_i F₀ := W_i F₀ / W_{i−1} F₀ is pure of weight i for every i. W_i F₀ is the largest perverse subsheaf of weights ≤ i, and F₀ / W_i F₀ has weights > i. Every morphism f : F₀ → G₀ of mixed perverse sheaves is strictly compatible: f(W_i F₀) = f(F₀) ∩ W_i G₀. The filtration is an arithmetic object on X₀; its arithmetic filtration need not split, and its geometric pullback can also be nonsplit, although each geometric graded piece is semisimple (EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity).
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Weights are integers (mixed in the sense of the Weil II weight convention, not ι-mixed with real weights); for ι-mixed objects BBD 5.3.5 applies to the weight-class decomposition modulo ℤ first.
proofSteps: Perv_m(X₀) is abelian with all objects of finite length (EDC.7/mixed-perverse-sheaves, EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification), and simple objects are pure (EDC.7/simple-mixed-perverse-is-pure).
For each i, partition the simple classes into S⁺ (weight > i) and S⁻ (weight ≤ i); Ext¹(V, U) = 0 for U ∈ S⁺, V ∈ S⁻ by EDC.7/weight-ext-vanishing (c).
EDC.7/torsion-theory-splitting-lemma gives the unique W_i F₀ with constituents of weight ≤ i and quotient with constituents of weight > i, and strictness.

An object of A⁻ has weights ≤ i (weights ≤ i are stable under extensions, EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes) and conversely constituents of an object of weights ≤ i have weights ≤ i (EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability); so W_i F₀ is the largest subobject of weights ≤ i and Gr^W_i is pure of weight i (BBD 5.3.5).
acceptance: For F₀ pure of weight w: W_{w−1}F₀ = 0 and W_w F₀ = F₀.

On 𝔾_{m,𝔽_q} with j : 𝔾_m ↪ 𝔸¹, the perverse sheaf Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] sits in 0 → ℚ̄_ℓ,𝔸¹[1] → Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] → δ₀(−1) → 0; its weight filtration has Gr_1 = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] and Gr_2 = δ₀(−1), the punctual sheaf at 0 of weight 2.

uses.how: the generic weight criterion and geometric semisimplicity use a simple quotient of maximal weight provided by W
W_{≤0} of cohomology of a filtered perverse sheaf is used to cut long exact sequences by weight
pure Satake objects have a one-step weight filtration, so semisimplicity applies directly

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_mono

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_eq_bot

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightGraded_isPure

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_unique

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_strict
api.statement: For f : F₀ → G₀, f(W_i F₀) = f(F₀) ∩ W_i G₀; in particular f maps W_i into W_i.

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_eq_largest
api.statement: W_i F₀ is the largest perverse subsheaf of F₀ having weights ≤ i.

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_dual

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_pure
tests.statement: If F₀ is pure of weight w then W_i F₀ = 0 for i < w and W_i F₀ = F₀ for i ≥ w.

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_jstar_Gm
tests.statement: For j : 𝔾_m ↪ 𝔸¹ over 𝔽_q, W_1(Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1]) = ℚ̄_ℓ,𝔸¹[1] and Gr^W_2(Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1]) ≅ δ₀(−1).

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_point
tests.statement: On Spec 𝔽_q, W_i of a mixed representation V is the sum of the generalized Frobenius eigenspaces with eigenvalues of weight ≤ i. The ordinary and perverse hearts on a point coincide; EDC.7/weight-endomorphism-weights supplies the spectral calculation.

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.weightFiltration_not_split_geometrically_trivial

sources.locator: Théorème 5.3.5 and its proof with Lemme 5.3.6, pp. 136–137
sources.match: BBD construct the unique finite increasing weight filtration with pure graded pieces and prove strict compatibility of morphisms, from Ext¹-vanishing between simple pure objects of decreasing weight and the abstract splitting lemma.

nodes.title: Upper weights of a mixed perverse sheaf are detected generically on closed subvarieties
nodes.statement: A mixed perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ has weights ≤ w iff every irreducible closed subscheme Y₀ ⊆ X₀, of dimension d, has a dense open U₀ ⊆ Y₀ on which the ordinary cohomology sheaf ℋ^{−d}(F₀)|_{U₀} has punctual weights ≤ w − d.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: Necessity: weights ≤ w means ℋ^{−d} has punctual weights ≤ w − d everywhere.

Sufficiency: otherwise, by EDC.7/weight-filtration, F₀ has a simple quotient G₀ pure of weight w′ > w, of the form j_!*(L₀[d]) on a smooth affine connected U₀ ⊂ Y₀ with L₀ punctually pure of weight w′ − d (EDC.7/simple-mixed-perverse-is-pure).

The long exact cohomology sequence of 0 → Ker → F₀ → G₀ → 0 gives, on a dense open of Y₀, a surjection ℋ^{−d}(F₀) → ℋ^{−d}(G₀) = L₀ (degree −d is the top degree there by the perverse stalk bounds, EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure); so L₀ has weights ≤ w − d, contradicting w′ > w (BBD 5.3.7).
acceptance: For F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] ⊕ δ₀(−1) on 𝔸¹: on Y₀ = 𝔸¹ the generic sheaf ℋ^{−1} = ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0 ≤ w − 1 iff w ≥ 1, and on Y₀ = {0} the sheaf ℋ^0 contains ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) of weight 2 ≤ w iff w ≥ 2; so F₀ has weights ≤ 2 and not ≤ 1.

sources.match: BBD: a mixed perverse sheaf has weights ≤ w iff on a dense open of each irreducible d-dimensional closed subvariety the cohomology sheaf in degree −d has punctual weights ≤ w − d.

nodes.title: Semisimple and geometrically semisimple perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: An object of an abelian category is semisimple if it is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of simple objects. A perverse sheaf F on X (over 𝔽̄_q) is semisimple if it is semisimple in Perv(X, ℚ̄_ℓ); then F ≅ ⊕_k i_{V_k*} j_{k!*}(L_k[d_k]) with V_k smooth connected locally closed of dimension d_k and L_k irreducible lisse. A perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ is geometrically semisimple if its pullback F to X is semisimple; a complex K₀ ∈ D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) is geometrically split-semisimple if its pullback K satisfies K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(K)[−i] with every pH^i(K) semisimple. No condition on the Frobenius structure is imposed.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Semisimplicity is a property of the geometric object over 𝔽̄_q, not of F₀ in Perv(X₀); a decomposition of K is an isomorphism, not a canonical one.
proofSteps: Finite direct sums exist in Perv(X) (an additive heart); finite length makes 'sum of simple subobjects' and 'finite direct sum of simples' agree.
The description of simple objects is EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification.

For lisse sheaves on a smooth connected X₀ shifted by dim X₀, the definition agrees with geometric semisimplicity of Geometric monodromy and geometrically semisimple lisse sheaves (EDC.7 weight foundations), since L ↦ L[d] is an exact fully faithful embedding of lisse sheaves into Perv(X) whose essential image is closed under subquotients on smooth X.
acceptance: The constant sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ[d] on a smooth connected X₀ of pure dimension d is geometrically semisimple. It is geometrically simple when X₀ is geometrically connected; for X₀ = Spec 𝔽_(q²), its geometric pullback is the direct sum of the constant sheaves on two points.
The arithmetic sheaf E₂ (unipotent Frobenius) on Spec 𝔽_q is geometrically semisimple (over 𝔽̄_q it is ℚ̄_ℓ²) but not semisimple in Perv(Spec 𝔽_q).

uses.how: the conclusion of the decomposition theorem is geometric split-semisimplicity
semisimplicity of the Satake category over 𝔽̄_q, used to show the Tannakian group is reductive
the Hitchin direct image over the elliptic locus is a direct sum of shifted simple perverse sheaves whose supports are then studied
endomorphisms of a middle-extension direct image are determined on a dense open

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.IsSemisimpleObject

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.IsSemisimpleObject.biprod

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.IsSemisimpleObject.of_mono

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.isSemisimpleObject_iff_socle

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.IsGeometricallySemisimple

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.IsGeometricallySemisimple.baseChange
api.statement: Geometric semisimplicity is invariant under extension of 𝔽_q to 𝔽_{qⁿ} and of E to E′.

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.isSemisimpleObject_moduleCat_field
tests.statement: For a field K, every finite-dimensional object of ModuleCat K is IsSemisimpleObject, agreeing with Mathlib's IsSemisimpleModule.

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.not_isSemisimpleObject_unipotent
tests.statement: The ℚ̄_ℓ[ℤ]-module ℚ̄_ℓ² on which 1 acts by the unipotent Jordan block is not semisimple in finite-dimensional ℤ-representations: its unique simple subobject has no complement.

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.E2_isGeometricallySemisimple
tests.statement: The rank-two unipotent sheaf E₂ on Spec 𝔽_q is geometrically semisimple, and its arithmetic object is not semisimple in Perv(Spec 𝔽_q).

sources.locator: Théorème 5.3.8 (statement), p. 138; 6.2.4 (the notion 'semi-simple' for complexes), p. 163
sources.match: BBD's conclusion that F over 𝔽̄_q is a direct sum of simple perverse sheaves j_!*L[d], and their definition of a semisimple complex as the sum of its shifted semisimple perverse cohomology sheaves.

nodes.title: Pure perverse sheaves are geometrically semisimple

planet.name: Geometric semisimplicity of pure perverse sheaves

nodes.statement: If F₀ is a pure perverse sheaf on X₀ (of some weight w), then F₀ is geometrically semisimple: over 𝔽̄_q, F is a finite direct sum of simple perverse sheaves i_*j_!*(L[d]) with L irreducible lisse on smooth connected U ⊂ X of dimension d. Neither F₀ in Perv(X₀) nor the Frobenius action is asserted semisimple.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Purity of the arithmetic object F₀ is the hypothesis; a perverse sheaf over 𝔽̄_q with no pure model is not covered.
proofSteps: Let F′ ⊆ F be the socle (sum of simple perverse subsheaves); it is Frobenius-stable, so it descends to F′₀ ⊆ F₀ (EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves, stability under subquotients).
F′₀ and F″₀ := F₀ / F′₀ are pure of weight w (EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability).
The class of 0 → F′₀ → F₀ → F″₀ → 0 in Hom^1(F″₀, F′₀) maps to zero in Hom^1(F″, F′) (EDC.7/weight-ext-vanishing (b)), so F ≅ F′ ⊕ F″ over 𝔽̄_q.
If F″ ≠ 0 it has a simple subobject, which lifts to a simple subobject of F not in F′, contradicting maximality; so F = F′ is semisimple (BBD 5.3.8, copying Weil II 3.4.1(iii)).
acceptance: Deligne's semisimplicity theorem: pure lisse sheaves are geometrically semisimple (EDC.7 weight foundations) (a punctually pure lisse sheaf on a normal X₀ is geometrically semisimple) is recovered for smooth connected X₀ by applying the theorem to L₀[dim X₀].
E₂ on Spec 𝔽_q is pure of weight 0 and geometrically semisimple, but F₀ = E₂ is not semisimple: the theorem asserts nothing about the arithmetic category.

sources.match: BBD prove that a pure perverse sheaf becomes a direct sum of simple perverse sheaves over 𝔽̄_q, by descending the socle and killing the extension class with 5.1.15(iii).
The lisse case on a normal base, whose proof BBD copy.

nodes.title: Indecomposable pure perverse sheaves are Jordan blocks on simple ones
nodes.statement: (a) The indecomposable pure perverse sheaves on X₀ with ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients are exactly S₀ ⊗ E_n with S₀ pure simple and n ≥ 1, where E_n is the pullback to X₀ of the rank-n sheaf on Spec 𝔽_q on which geometric Frobenius acts unipotently with one Jordan block. (b) If S₀ is simple, there are d ≥ 1 and a perverse sheaf S₁ on X₁ := X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{q^d} such that S₀ ≅ π_*S₁ for π : X₁ → X₀, S₁ is geometrically simple (its pullback to X is simple) and S₁ is not isomorphic to any of its nonidentity conjugates under Gal(𝔽_{q^d}/𝔽_q). Part (a) also holds with coefficients a finite E/ℚ_ℓ; part (b) does not in general.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: For F₀ with F semisimple (e.g. F₀ pure, EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity), decompose F into isotypic components indexed by isomorphism classes a of simple constituents; Frobenius permutes the classes, and orbits C give a decomposition F₀ = ⊕_C F₀,C descending by EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves.
For an orbit of length d, the a-part is defined over 𝔽_{q^d} and F₀,C ≅ π_*(F₁,a); choose φ : Fr^{d*}G_a ≅ G_a for a simple G_a; then F₁,a ≅ G_a ⊗ V_a with V_a := Hom(G_a, F_a) carrying a Frobenius.

Indecomposability forces one orbit and a single Jordan block on V_a; rescaling φ makes it unipotent, giving S₀ ⊗ E_n with S₀ = π_*(G₁) simple (BBD 5.3.9(i)); for F₀ simple, V_a is one-dimensional, giving (b).

With E coefficients the linear algebra of 5.3.9(i) still goes through, but the descent of a geometrically simple constituent to a finite extension may need a coefficient extension, so (b) fails as stated (BBD 5.3.10).
acceptance: E_n on Spec 𝔽_q is pure of weight 0 and indecomposable but not simple for n ≥ 2.

Let X₀ = Spec 𝔽_{q²}, viewed over 𝔽_q: the simple perverse sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ on X₀ pulls back to ℚ̄_ℓ ⊕ ℚ̄_ℓ on the two geometric points, so it is not geometrically simple; it is π_*S₁ for d = 2 and S₁ the constant sheaf on one of the two components of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{q²}, which is geometrically simple and not isomorphic to its Galois conjugate.

sources.match: BBD classify indecomposable pure perverse sheaves as tensor products of simple ones with unipotent Jordan blocks, describe simple ones by induction from a finite extension, and note what survives with E_λ coefficients.

nodes.title: A pure perverse sheaf splits into an intermediate extension and a part supported on the complement
nodes.statement: Let F₀ be a pure perverse sheaf on X₀, j : U₀ ↪ X₀ open and i : Z₀ ↪ X₀ the complementary closed immersion. Then F₀ has a unique decomposition F₀ = j_!*F′₀ ⊕ i_*F″₀ in Perv(X₀), with F′₀ = j^*F₀; the adjunction map pj_!j^*F₀ → F₀ factors through the quotient j_!*j^*F₀ of pj_!j^*F₀, the map F₀ → pj_*j^*F₀ through the subobject j_!*j^*F₀ of pj_*j^*F₀, and the composite of adjunction maps i_* pH⁰(i^!F₀) → F₀ → i_* pH⁰(i^*F₀) is an isomorphism (both sides equal i_*F″₀).
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
F₀ pure; for mixed F₀ the decomposition fails (e.g. Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on 𝔸¹).
proofSteps: Uniqueness: Hom(j_!*F′, i_*F″) = Hom(i_*F″, j_!*F′) = 0 since j_!* has no subobject or quotient supported on Z (EDC.5/recollement-intermediate-extension).
By EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves it suffices to check the factorisations and that the maps are the inclusions and projections of a decomposition over 𝔽̄_q.

Over 𝔽̄_q, F is semisimple (EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity), so it suffices to treat its simple constituents, each of the form j_!*G′ or i_*G″ (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification), for which the statements are immediate (BBD 5.3.11).
acceptance: For the mixed, not pure, perverse sheaf F₀ = Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on 𝔸¹_{𝔽_q} with Z = {0}: i^!F₀ = 0 while pH⁰(i^*F₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) ≠ 0, so the composite in the statement is not an isomorphism, and F₀ is a non-split extension of δ₀(−1) by ℚ̄_ℓ[1]; purity is necessary.
For F₀ = IC_{X₀} with X₀ irreducible and U₀ dense, F″₀ = 0.

sources.locator: Corollaire 5.3.11, p. 140 (checked on the page image)
sources.match: BBD: a pure perverse sheaf has a unique decomposition j_!*F′ ⊕ i_*F″, with the adjunction maps factoring through the intermediate extension and i_*pi^!F → F → i_*pi^*F an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Weights of a mixed complex are read off its perverse cohomology
nodes.statement: Let K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ). (a) K₀ has weights ≤ w (resp. ≥ w) iff every perverse cohomology sheaf pH^i(K₀) has weights ≤ w + i (resp. ≥ w + i). (b) K₀ is pure of weight w iff every pH^i(K₀) is pure of weight w + i. (c) For f : X₀ → Y₀ of finite type and F₀ a mixed perverse sheaf of weights ≤ w, the perverse sheaves pH⁰(Rf_!F₀) and pH⁰(f^*F₀) have weights ≤ w; if F₀ has weights ≥ w, pH⁰(Rf_*F₀) and pH⁰(Rf^!F₀) have weights ≥ w.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Perverse truncation and perverse cohomology are those of EDC.7/mixed-perverse-sheaves; the shift convention puts pH^i(K₀)[−i] in weights ≤ w + i − i = w when pH^i has weights ≤ w + i.
proofSteps: Sufficiency in (a): weights ≤ w are stable under extensions in triangles (EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes); use the triangles (pτ_{<i}K₀, pτ_{≤i}K₀, pH^i(K₀)[−i]).

Necessity for upper bounds is BBD 5.4.1, by descending induction, reducing to w=0 and pH⁰K₀. Once the positive perverse cohomology is bounded, pτ≤0K₀ has upper weight ≤0. On an irreducible d-dimensional closed Y₀ use the exact sequence ℋ⁻ᵈ(pτ≤0K₀)|_Y₀ → ℋ⁻ᵈ(pH⁰K₀)|_Y₀ → ℋ⁻ᵈ⁺¹(pτ<0K₀)|_Y₀. The last term vanishes on a dense open by the perverse support condition, so the middle term is generically a quotient of the first, whose punctual weights are ≤−d. Apply the generic-weight criterion. Duality gives lower bounds. The first term is not claimed to vanish.
(b) is (a) applied to both bounds (BBD 5.4.4).
(c): Rf_!, f^* preserve upper bounds and Rf_*, f^! lower bounds (Weight estimates for the six operations (EDC.7 weight foundations)); apply (a) to the degree-0 perverse cohomology (BBD 5.4.2).
acceptance: For X₀ smooth of dimension d, K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ (weight 0): pH^d(K₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ[d] is pure of weight 0 + d, and all other pH^i vanish.

For f : 𝔸¹_{𝔽_q} → Spec 𝔽_q and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] (pure of weight 1): Rf_!F₀ = H²_c(𝔸¹)[−1] = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[−1], whose only perverse cohomology sheaf pH¹ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weight 2 = 1 + 1; by (b), Rf_!F₀ is pure of weight 1.

sources.match: BBD: K₀ has weights ≤ w (≥ w) iff each pH^iK₀ has weights ≤ w + i (≥ w + i); hence perverse cohomology of a pure complex is pure, and pH⁰ of f_!, f^* (f_*, f^!) preserve upper (lower) weight bounds.

nodes.title: Intermediate extension along a quasi-finite morphism preserves weights
nodes.statement: Let f : X₀ → Y₀ be quasi-finite (for example any locally closed immersion) and F₀ a mixed perverse sheaf on X₀. Define f_!*F₀ := Im(pH⁰(Rf_!F₀) → pH⁰(Rf_*F₀)). If F₀ has weights ≥ w (resp. ≤ w), so does f_!*F₀; pure perverse sheaves go to pure perverse sheaves of the same weight. For a locally closed immersion j this is the intermediate extension j_!* of EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension, without the affineness hypothesis of EDC.7/intersection-complex-purity.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
f quasi-finite and separated of finite type.
proofSteps: pH⁰(Rf_!F₀) has weights ≤ w when F₀ does and pH⁰(Rf_*F₀) has weights ≥ w when F₀ does (EDC.7/perverse-cohomology-weights (c)).
f_!*F₀ is a quotient of the first and a subobject of the second, so EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability gives both bounds (BBD 5.4.3, following the first proof of 5.3.2).
For an immersion, the image of pH⁰j_! → pH⁰j_* is j_!* (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension, BBD 1.4.22).
acceptance: For j : 𝔸² ∖ {0} ↪ 𝔸² (quasi-finite, not affine), Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[2] is not perverse (it has the cohomology sheaf δ₀(−2) in degree 1), but the image of pH⁰(Rj_!ℚ̄_ℓ[2]) → pH⁰(Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[2]) is j_!*ℚ̄_ℓ[2] = ℚ̄_ℓ[2], pure of weight 2.
For f finite (e.g. a normalisation), f_!* = f_* is exact and preserves purity.

sources.match: BBD: for quasi-finite f, f_!* = Im(pf_! → pf_*) carries perverse sheaves of weights ≥ w (≤ w) to perverse sheaves of weights ≥ w (≤ w), hence pure to pure of the same weight.

nodes.title: Pure complexes split geometrically into shifted intersection complexes
nodes.statement: Let K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) be pure of weight w. Then over 𝔽̄_q: (a) K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(K)[−i] (a finite sum, isomorphism in D^b_c(X, ℚ̄_ℓ)); (b) each pH^i(K) is semisimple, being the pullback of the pure perverse sheaf pH^i(K₀) of weight w + i; (c) consequently K ≅ ⊕_k (i_{V_k*} j_{k!*}(L_k[d_k]))[n_k] for finitely many smooth connected locally closed V_k of dimension d_k, irreducible lisse L_k on V_k and integers n_k. The isomorphism in (a) is not canonical and need not be compatible with the Frobenius structure of K₀.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Purity of the arithmetic complex K₀ is required; the conclusion is over 𝔽̄_q only.
proofSteps: pH^i(K₀) is pure of weight w + i (EDC.7/perverse-cohomology-weights (b)), so pH^i(K₀)[−i] is pure of weight w and pτ_{<i}K₀ has weights ≤ w, pH^i(K₀)[−i] weights ≥ w.

The connecting morphism of (pτ_{<i}K₀, pτ_{≤i}K₀, pH^i(K₀)[−i]) is a degree-one map from pH^i(K₀)[−i] to pτ_{<i}K₀; by EDC.7/weight-ext-vanishing (b) its image over 𝔽̄_q is zero, so pτ_{≤i}K ≅ pτ_{<i}K ⊕ pH^i(K)[−i]; induct on i (BBD 5.4.5).
(b) is EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity; (c) combines (a), (b) and the classification of simple perverse sheaves (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification) (BBD 5.4.6).
acceptance: For X₀ smooth projective, K₀ = Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ for f : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q is pure of weight 0 and the splitting is H*(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) ≅ ⊕_i H^i(X)[−i], the elementary decomposition of a complex of vector spaces.

Arithmetic perverse-cohomology splitting can fail: on X₀=𝔸¹ set G₀=ℚ̄_ℓ[1] and F₀=δ₀(−1). Geometrically Hom¹(F,G)=ℚ̄_ℓ with trivial Frobenius and Hom²(F,G)=0; adic Hochschild–Serre gives Ext²_X₀(F₀,G₀)=ℚ̄_ℓ. A nonzero class defines G₀ → K₀ → F₀[−1] → G₀[1]. Its perverse cohomology has weights 1 in degree 0 and 2 in degree 1, so K₀ is pure of weight 1. The triangle splits geometrically but not arithmetically. Separately, E₂ on a point obstructs splitting into arithmetic simple constituents, not splitting into perverse cohomology degrees.

sources.match: BBD: a pure complex over 𝔽_q splits over 𝔽̄_q as the sum of its shifted perverse cohomology sheaves (by 5.4.4 and 5.1.15(iii)), hence as a sum of shifted j_!*L[d] with L irreducible lisse.

nodes.title: The decomposition theorem for proper morphisms over finite fields
nodes.statement: Let f₀ : X₀ → Y₀ be a proper morphism of separated schemes of finite type over 𝔽_q and K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) pure of weight w (for example K₀ = IC_{X₀}(L₀) with L₀ lisse punctually pure of weight w − dim X₀ on a smooth dense open, or K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[dim X₀] for X₀ smooth). Then: (a) Rf₀_*K₀ is pure of weight w and each pH^i(Rf₀_*K₀) is pure of weight w + i; (b) over 𝔽̄_q, Rf_*K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(Rf_*K)[−i]; (c) each pH^i(Rf_*K) is semisimple, a finite sum of i_{V*}j_!*(L[dim V]) with L irreducible lisse on smooth connected V ⊂ Y; (d) for Y₀ proper over 𝔽_q, H^j(Y, Rf_*K) = H^j(X, K) is pure of weight w + j. No integral or mod-ℓ decomposition, no canonical or Frobenius-compatible splitting, and no semisimplicity of the arithmetic Frobenius is asserted.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
f₀ proper; K₀ pure (a pure arithmetic model is part of the input).
proofSteps: (a): proper direct image preserves purity (Proper direct images of pure complexes are pure (EDC.7 weight foundations)); perverse cohomology of a pure complex is pure (EDC.7/perverse-cohomology-weights (b)).
(b), (c): apply EDC.7/pure-complex-geometric-splitting to Rf₀_*K₀.
(d): compose with the proper structure map of Y₀ and use (a) for Y₀ → Spec 𝔽_q.
The standard inputs IC_{X₀}(L₀) pure of weight w come from EDC.7/intersection-complex-purity.
acceptance: For the blow-up π : X₀ → 𝔸²_{𝔽_q} of the origin, Rπ_*ℚ̄_ℓ[2] ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ δ₀(−1) over 𝔽̄_q, both summands pure of weight 2 (the exceptional ℙ¹ contributes H²(ℙ¹) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) at 0).
For f : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q proper and K₀ = IC_{X₀}, (d) gives purity of intersection cohomology, agreeing with EDC.7/intersection-complex-purity (c).

The finite-type proper models and resolutions over 𝔽̄_q used by GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS3–GS4 (Zhu, proof of Lemma 2.11) and the proper Hitchin-type maps of ET.2b are instances, with the purity of their inputs established by the consumer.

For Zhu’s resolution in §2.1, Lemma 2.11, pp.26–27, use π_*ℚ̄_ℓ[d] = IC_μ ⊕ C. The working IC shift is [d], as in the main text §2.1.1 p.20; Appendix A.3.1 p.55 prints the dualizing shift [2d](d), the known normalization misprint PAPER-ZHU-17/E25. The perfect-space transport remains a Part II input.

sources.match: BBD's pure-complex decomposition applied to proper direct images, which preserve purity.
Proper direct images of pure complexes are pure.

sources.locator: proof of Lemma 2.11, p. 26 (arXiv v3); Appendix A.3.1, pp. 54–55
sources.match: Zhu applies the decomposition theorem to proper maps between finite-type models of Witt-vector affine Schubert varieties, the finite-type instance routed here (PAPER-ZHU-17/E06).
Yun–Zhang use that the relevant direct-image perverse sheaves are pure of weight 0 and the resulting weight splitting of cohomology sequences (PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19/11).

nodes.title: The decomposition theorem for semismall maps
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be smooth over 𝔽_q of pure dimension n, f₀ : X₀ → Y₀ proper and surjective, and assume f is semismall: dim(X ×_Y X) ≤ n. Choose a stratification of Y₀ into smooth connected locally closed strata S₀ (defined over 𝔽_q after a finite extension) such that each R^q f_*ℚ̄_ℓ restricted to each stratum is lisse; put d_S := dim f^{−1}(y) for y ∈ S, and call S relevant if dim S + 2 d_S = n. Then Rf₀_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] is a pure perverse sheaf of weight n, and over 𝔽̄_q there is an isomorphism Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] ≅ ⊕_{S relevant} IC_{S̄}(L_S), L_S := (R^{2d_S}f_*ℚ̄_ℓ)|_S, where L_S is the lisse sheaf whose geometric fibre at y is H^{2d_S}(f^{−1}(y)) ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ(−d_S)^{#(top-dimensional irreducible components of f^{−1}(y))}. The summand supported on S̄ (its S-isotypic part for the support decomposition) is canonically determined.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
X₀ smooth of pure dimension n; f₀ proper surjective and semismall; the stratification makes all R^q f_*ℚ̄_ℓ lisse on strata.

Choose a finite algebraic stratification adapted to f, with the fibre dimension locally constant on each stratum and the frontier condition; test semismallness on that stratification. The complex-topological semismall theorem is a comparison source; the étale statement uses the support estimate, Verdier duality and the scheme decomposition theorem.
proofSteps: Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] is perverse by the smooth-source constant-coefficient semismall criterion (the special case stated in EDC.5/semismall-pushforward-perversity; de Cataldo–Migliorini Proposition 4.2.1), and pure of weight n by Purity on a smooth scheme is pointwise purity of lisse cohomology sheaves (EDC.7 weight foundations) (c) and Proper direct images of pure complexes are pure (EDC.7 weight foundations).

By EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity, Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] = ⊕ IC_{S̄}(M_S) over 𝔽̄_q, grouping simple constituents by the stratum of the generic point of their support, with M_S semisimple lisse on S (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification).
Restrict to a stratum S: an IC_{S̄′}(M_{S′}) with S ⊂ S̄′ ∖ S′ has ℋ^j vanishing on S for j ≥ −dim S (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension stalk bound), so ℋ^{−dim S}(Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n])|_S = M_S.

By proper base change the left side is R^{n−dim S}f_*ℚ̄_ℓ|_S, whose fibres are H^{n−dim S}(f^{−1}(y)); semismallness gives n − dim S ≥ 2 d_S, so it vanishes unless S is relevant, where it is the top cohomology H^{2d_S}(f^{−1}(y)) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−d_S)^{#top components} (EDC.2:trace-purity/top-degree-compact-cohomology).
The support decomposition of a semisimple perverse sheaf is canonical (the S-part is the sum of all simple subobjects with generic support point in S).
acceptance: For the blow-up of 𝔸² at the origin (n = 2): strata 𝔸²∖{0} (d = 0, relevant) and {0} (d = 1, 0 + 2 = 2, relevant), giving ℚ̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ δ₀(−1), matching EDC.7/decomposition-theorem's acceptance example.
For a small map (all non-dense strata irrelevant) the formula reduces to Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] ≅ IC_Y(L) with L = f_*ℚ̄_ℓ on the dense stratum, agreeing with EDC.5/small-pushforward-intersection-complex.

For the Springer resolution (with characteristic different from 2 in the SL₂ example) of the nilpotent cone of SL₂ (n = 2), the strata are the regular orbit (d = 0) and the origin (d = 1, relevant), giving ℚ̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ δ₀(−1) as for the A₁ surface singularity.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.2.1, Definitions 4.2.2–4.2.3, Remark 4.2.4 and Theorem 4.2.7, pp. 55–57 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: de Cataldo and Migliorini characterise semismall maps by perversity of f_*Q[n], define relevant strata, and state the semismall decomposition f_*Q_X[n] ≅ ⊕ IC_S(L_S) with L_S the monodromy of top-dimensional fibre components, over ℂ; the étale argument here follows the same support count.

nodes.title: Graded Lefschetz objects and primitive parts in an abelian category with a Tate twist
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian category with an additive autoequivalence M ↦ M(1) and powers M(n), n ∈ ℤ. A graded Lefschetz object (L, η) consists of objects L^i ∈ A for i ∈ ℤ, zero outside a finite interval, and morphisms η_i : L^i → L^{i+2}(1). For r ≥ 0 its iterate η^r : L^{i} → L^{i+2r}(r) is η_{i+2r−2}(r−1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ η_i(0), with the canonical identifications (a)(b) ≅ (a+b). (L, η) satisfies hard Lefschetz if η^r : L^{−r} → L^{r}(r) is an isomorphism for every r ≥ 0. Its primitive part in degree −r ≤ 0 is the kernel P^{−r} := ker(η^{r+1} : L^{−r} → L^{r+2}(r+1)), with its inclusion into L^{−r}.
hypotheses: A abelian; (1) an additive autoequivalence with chosen coherence isomorphisms (a)(b) ≅ (a + b); in the application A = Perv(Y₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) or Perv(Y, ℚ̄_ℓ) and (1) is the Tate twist.
proofSteps: The iterate is defined by induction on r, composing with the twisted η and the coherence isomorphisms; hard Lefschetz and primitive parts are defined from it with Mathlib's kernels.
Morphisms of graded Lefschetz objects are families of morphisms commuting with η; kernels of η-iterates are functorial for them.
acceptance: For A = finite-dimensional ℚ̄_ℓ-vector spaces with trivial twist, L^i = H^{n+i}(X) of a smooth projective n-dimensional X and η = cup product with an ample class, this is the data of The Lefschetz operator of a line bundle (EDC.7 weight foundations), and P^{−r} is the primitive cohomology P^{n−r}.

uses.how: the perverse cohomology sheaves pH^i(Rf_*F₀) with η = c₁ of a relatively ample line bundle form a graded Lefschetz object in Perv(Y₀)
primitive parts give the relative Lefschetz decomposition of perverse cohomology

uses.where: Primitive decomposition for a graded operator satisfying hard Lefschetz (EDC.7 weight foundations)
uses.how: the vector-space case with trivial twist is DWP.9's graded operator
