nodes.title: Primitive decomposition of a graded Lefschetz object satisfying hard Lefschetz
nodes.statement: Let (L, η) be a graded Lefschetz object in an abelian category with Tate twist (EDC.7/graded-lefschetz-object) satisfying hard Lefschetz. Then for every r ≥ 0 the map ⊕_{a ≥ 0} P^{−r−2a}(−a) → L^{−r}, given on the a-th summand by η^a composed with the primitive inclusion and the twist coherence, is an isomorphism (a finite biproduct), and for every r ≥ 0, L^{r} ≅ L^{−r}(−r) via η^r. Equivalently, in each degree n the map from the biproduct of the primitive string columns P^{−r}(−a), 0 ≤ a ≤ r, −r + 2a = n, to L^n is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Hard Lefschetz for all r ≥ 0; L of finite support. No splitting is assumed: the summands are the actual kernels and the maps are actual η-powers.
proofSteps: For r ≥ 0, η : L^{−r−2} → L^{−r}(1) is a monomorphism, since η^{r+1} ∘ η = η^{r+2} is an isomorphism on L^{−r−2}.

Make every twist explicit. On L⁻ʳ the projection to the nonprimitive summand is p = η(−1) ∘ (η^(r+2))⁻¹(−1) ∘ η^(r+1): the successive objects are L^(r+2)(r+1), L^(−r−2)(−1), L⁻ʳ. Hard Lefschetz makes p an idempotent whose image is η(L^(−r−2)(−1)) and whose kernel is P⁻ʳ. The abelian splitting of this idempotent yields L⁻ʳ ≅ P⁻ʳ ⊕ L^(−r−2)(−1). The additive autoequivalence and its inverse preserve kernels and this splitting.
Iterate (induction on the length of the support) to obtain the full string decomposition; positive degrees follow from the isomorphisms η^r.
acceptance: In the vector-space case the statement is Primitive decomposition for a graded operator satisfying hard Lefschetz (EDC.7 weight foundations) (i)–(ii), including dim P^{n−r} = dim V^{n−r} − dim V^{n−r−2}.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.2.1, item 2 (primitive Lefschetz decomposition), pp. 81–82 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: The primitive decomposition derived formally from hard Lefschetz; the argument uses only kernels, images and the inverse of η^r, so it holds in any abelian category with a twist.
The hard-Lefschetz input in the perverse setting, from which the decomposition is formal.

nodes.title: Perverse cohomology along the universal hyperplane section
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y factor as a closed immersion X ↪ ℙ^d × Y followed by the projection, with η = c₁(𝒪(1)). Let Y′ = ℙ^{d∨} × Y, X′ = ℙ^{d∨} × X with u : X′ → X and u : Y′ → Y the projections (smooth of relative dimension d with connected fibres), H ⊂ X′ the universal hyperplane section, v : H ↪ X′ and h : H → Y′ the induced proper map. For K ∈ pD^{≥0}(X): (i) u^*Rf_*K ≅ Rf′_*u^*K, hence (u^*pH^i Rf_*K)[d] ≅ pH^{i+d}(Rf′_*u^*K); (ii) for i < d − 1, pH^i(Rf′_*u^*K) ≅ pH^i(Rh_*(uv)^*K); (iii) pH^{d−1}(Rf′_*u^*K) → pH^{d−1}(Rh_*(uv)^*K) is injective and identifies the source with the largest perverse subsheaf of the target that comes from Y (is of the form u^*G[d]).
hypotheses: X, Y separated of finite type over a field k (k = 𝔽_q or 𝔽̄_q), coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ; the factorisation through ℙ^d × Y is available locally on Y after replacing η by a multiple.
proofSteps: u is smooth of relative dimension d with connected fibres, so u^*[d] is t-exact and fully faithful on perverse sheaves, with a largest subobject and a largest quotient coming from Y (EDC.5/smooth-pullback-perverse-exactness, BBD 4.2.4–4.2.6); smooth base change gives (i).

u^*K lies in pD^{≥d}(X′); the projection g : U := X′ ∖ H → Y′ is affine, so g_!(u^*K|_U) ∈ pD^{≥d}(Y′) by left t-exactness of g_! (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing, BBD 4.1.2); the triangle (g_!(u^*K|_U), Rf′_*u^*K, Rh_*(uv)^*K) gives (ii) and the injectivity in (iii).

For (iii) it remains to compare pH^{−d}u_* of the two sides; by the projective-bundle formula (EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition, BBD 5.4.12) u_*u^* = ⊕_{i=0}^{d} (−)[−2i](−i) and (uv)_*(uv)^* has the same summands for i ≤ d − 1, and the fibre-dimension bound gives the needed vanishing (BBD 5.4.13).
acceptance: For Y a point and X = ℙ^d itself, H is the universal hyperplane (incidence variety) and (ii)–(iii) recover the weak Lefschetz statement for hyperplane sections of ℙ^d in degrees below d − 1.

sources.match: BBD's universal hyperplane section set-up, the comparison of perverse cohomology of f_*u^*K and h_*(uv)^*K in low degrees and in degree d − 1 (largest subobject coming from Y), via smooth pullback exactness, affine vanishing and the projective-bundle formula.

nodes.title: Relative hard Lefschetz
nodes.statement: Let f₀ : X₀ → Y₀ be a projective morphism of separated schemes of finite type over 𝔽_q and η ∈ H²(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ(1)) the first Chern class of an f₀-ample line bundle. Cup product with η gives η : K₀ → K₀[2](1) for every K₀, hence η^i : pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*K₀) → pH^{i}(Rf₀_*K₀)(i). If F₀ is a pure perverse sheaf on X₀ of weight w, then for every i ≥ 0, η^i : pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*F₀) → pH^{i}(Rf₀_*F₀)(i) is an isomorphism of pure perverse sheaves of weight w − i on Y₀ (the same then holds over 𝔽̄_q). A proper morphism has no automatic ample class: projectivity and the chosen relatively ample line bundle are hypotheses.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
f₀ projective; the line bundle is f₀-ample; η is its Chern class in the adic theory (EDC.3/chern-classes, EDC.6/adic-transport-of-duality-and-classes); F₀ pure perverse.
proofSteps: The question is local on Y₀; after shrinking Y₀ and replacing η by a positive multiple (which does not change bijectivity of η^i), f₀ factors through ℙ^d × Y₀ with η = c₁(𝒪(1)).
Case i = 1: η is the composite of restriction pH^{−1}(Rf_*F) → pH^0(Rh_*((uv)^*F[d−1])) along the universal hyperplane and its dual Gysin map back to pH^1(Rf_*F)(1) (after u^*[d]).
By EDC.7/universal-hyperplane-lemma, u^*pH^{−1} is the largest subobject of P := pH^0(Rh_*((uv)^*F[d−1])) coming from Y, and dually u^*pH^1(1) is its largest quotient coming from Y.

(uv)^*F₀[d−1] is pure (smooth pullback), so Rh_* of it and P are pure (Proper direct images of pure complexes are pure (EDC.7 weight foundations), EDC.7/perverse-cohomology-weights), hence P is semisimple over 𝔽̄_q (EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity); the largest sub coming from Y maps isomorphically to the largest such quotient, so η is an isomorphism (BBD 5.4.14).
General i: induction on i, factoring u^*[d] of η^{i+1} through pH^{−i}h_*, the inductive isomorphism for h and (uv)^*F[d−1], and the dual Gysin map (BBD 5.4.15).
Weights: pH^{−i} has weight w − i and pH^{i}(i) has weight w + i − 2i = w − i.
acceptance: For Y₀ = Spec 𝔽_q, X₀ smooth projective of dimension n and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[n], the statement is The hard Lefschetz theorem (EDC.7 weight foundations): η^i : H^{n−i}(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) ≅ H^{n+i}(X, ℚ̄_ℓ(i)).
For f₀ = ℙ¹ × Y₀ → Y₀ and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1 + dim Y₀] with Y₀ smooth: pH^{−1} = ℚ̄_ℓ[dim Y₀] and pH^{1} = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[dim Y₀], and η is the isomorphism given by the class of a point in H²(ℙ¹).

The ampleness hypothesis matters: for f : ℙ¹_{𝔽_q} → Spec 𝔽_q and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1], the trivial line bundle gives η = 0, so η¹ : pH^{−1} = H⁰(ℙ¹) → pH¹(1) = H²(ℙ¹)(1) is zero although both sides are ℚ̄_ℓ.

sources.locator: 5.4.10 (statement), p. 144; proof 5.4.14–5.4.15, pp. 146–147 (checked on the page images)
sources.match: BBD's relative hard Lefschetz for a projective morphism and a relatively ample class, proved by the universal hyperplane section, purity and geometric semisimplicity, and induction on i.
Survey statement of relative hard Lefschetz over 𝔽_q and 𝔽̄_q for pure perverse sheaves and its special case of hard Lefschetz in intersection cohomology.

nodes.title: Relative primitive decomposition of perverse cohomology
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem, put P^{−i} := ker(η^{i+1} : pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*F₀) → pH^{i+2}(Rf₀_*F₀)(i+1)) for i ≥ 0. Then for every i ≥ 0, pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*F₀) ≅ ⊕_{a ≥ 0} P^{−i−2a}(−a) via η-powers, in Perv(Y₀); and over 𝔽̄_q, Rf_*F ≅ ⊕_{i ≥ 0} ⊕_{a=0}^{i} P^{−i}(−a)[i − 2a] (non-canonically for the sum over degrees, by EDC.7/decomposition-theorem). Each P^{−i} is pure of weight w − i.
hypotheses: As in EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem.
proofSteps: The perverse cohomology sheaves with the η-maps form a graded Lefschetz object in Perv(Y₀) with the Tate twist (EDC.7/graded-lefschetz-object), which satisfies hard Lefschetz by EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem.
Apply EDC.7/abstract-primitive-decomposition in Perv(Y₀).
Combine with the geometric splitting of EDC.7/decomposition-theorem (b) for the statement on Rf_*F; purity of P^{−i} by EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability.
acceptance: For f the structure map of a smooth projective X₀ of dimension n and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[n], P^{−i} is primitive cohomology P^{n−i}(X), and the decomposition is the classical Lefschetz decomposition, matching EDC.7/abstract-primitive-decomposition.

sources.match: Hard Lefschetz on perverse cohomology, from which the primitive decomposition is formal.
Primitive decomposition from hard Lefschetz.

nodes.title: Hard Lefschetz in intersection cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be projective over 𝔽_q of pure dimension n, η the Chern class of an ample line bundle, and L₀ a lisse sheaf on a smooth dense open of X₀, punctually pure of weight w. Then for every i ≥ 0, cup product with η^i is an isomorphism IH^{n−i}(X, L) → IH^{n+i}(X, L)(i), where IH^j(X, L) := H^{j−n}(X, IC_X(L)), between spaces pure of weight w + n − i.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes and EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
X₀ projective; L₀ punctually pure (a pure model is required).
proofSteps: IC_{X₀}(L₀) is pure of weight w + n (EDC.7/intersection-complex-purity).
Apply EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem to f₀ : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q and F₀ = IC_{X₀}(L₀); perverse cohomology on a point is ordinary cohomology.
acceptance: For X₀ smooth projective and L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ this is The hard Lefschetz theorem (EDC.7 weight foundations) over 𝔽̄_q.
Agreement with Weil II 6.2.13 (Hard Lefschetz for potentially pure complexes (EDC.7 weight foundations)) for K = IC_X(L), whose support conditions hold with the integer n = dim X.

sources.locator: Théorème 5.4.10 with Y₀ a point, p. 144; 6.2.10, p. 165
sources.match: BBD note that the case of Y a point gives hard Lefschetz in intersection cohomology.
The case Y₀ = point, P₀ = IC gives hard Lefschetz for intersection cohomology over 𝔽_q and 𝔽̄_q.

nodes.title: Restricted constructible categories and their specialisation to finite fields
nodes.statement: Let X be of finite type over ℂ, T a finite stratification of X into smooth connected algebraic strata and, for each T ∈ T, L(T) a finite set of isomorphism classes of irreducible locally constant sheaves of ℤ/ℓ-modules on T. D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) is the full subcategory of D^b_c(X, ℤ_ℓ) of objects for which every ℋ^q(K⊗^Lℤ/ℓ)|_T is locally constant with all constituents in L(T), using the derived reduction of the complex K. Choose a finitely generated ℤ-subalgebra A ⊂ ℂ, S = Spec A, and a model (X_S, T_S, L_S) over S, shrunk so that strata are smooth over S with geometrically connected fibres and the relative sheaves Ext^q(j_!L,j′_!L′) commute with base change, and R^p a_*Ext^q(j_!L,j′_!L′) are locally constant on S and commute with base change, for a:X_S→S and the finitely many pairs under consideration. For a strictly henselian DVR V with A ⊂ V ⊂ ℂ whose residue field s̄ is an algebraic closure of a finite residue field of A, the restriction functors D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) ← D^b_{T,L}(X_V, ℤ_ℓ) → D^b_{T,L}(X_s̄, ℤ_ℓ) are equivalences; the induced system of equivalences D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) ≃ D^b_{T,L}(X_s̄, ℤ_ℓ), as a germ along the filter of such V, depends only on (X, T, L). After refining (T, L) and shrinking S, the equivalences respect any given finite list of the operations Rf_*, Rf_!, f^*, Rf^!, ⊗, RHom, the perverse t-structure (when the R^q j_*L|_{T′} are lisse with constituents in L(T′)), and rank, lissity and monodromy of sheaves on strata; they extend to ℚ_ℓ, E_λ and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients. There is no equivalence of the full categories D^b_c(X, ℤ_ℓ) ≃ D^b_c(X_s̄, ℤ_ℓ).
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
Only finitely many operations and objects are transported at a time; refinements change the germ only by restriction.
proofSteps: For ℤ/ℓⁿ coefficients the equivalences are formal from the identification of the H^p(−, Ext^q(F, G)) on X, X_V and X_s̄ for F, G of the form j_!L (smooth and proper base change on the chosen model, generic base change, SF.0 geometric spreading out and SF.2 cohomological base change) (BBD 6.1.9).

Finite Tor dimension is preserved, and the ℓ-adic statement follows from the definition of ℓ-adic derived categories as normalized systems (EDC.6/normalized-adic-system, EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories).

Compatibility with operations and with the perverse t-structure: enlarge (T, L) so that the operations send the restricted categories into restricted categories, then shrink S so that base change holds (BBD 6.1.10, using EGA IV §§8–9 spreading-out lists, 6.1.7).
Over ℂ, the étale category is compared with the analytic one by EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison.
acceptance: For X = a point and T = {X}, D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) is the category of perfect ℤ_ℓ-complexes, identical over ℂ and over s̄; for X = ℙ¹_ℂ with one stratum and L = {ℤ/ℓ}, the specialisation sends Rπ_*ℤ_ℓ to Rπ_*ℤ_ℓ on ℙ¹_{s̄}, both with cohomology ℤ_ℓ, 0, ℤ_ℓ(−1).

A non-quasi-unipotent ℤ_ℓ-local system on 𝔾_m still belongs to a restricted category: its finite-dimensional mod-ℓ representation has finitely many irreducible constituents, which can be chosen as L(T). BBD 6.1.8 warns that the entire ℓ-adic sheaf need not descend to a finitely generated field; the restricted-category specialization germ does not assert such descent.

the restricted categories are the carriers of the specialisation equivalences

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.GoodModel

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.specializationEquiv_comm

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.restrictedCategory_point

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.restrictedCategory_empty_L
tests.statement: If every L(T) is empty, derived reduction has zero cohomology on every stratum. Derived completeness and Nakayama force the object itself to be zero.

tests.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.restrictedCategory_excluded_character

nodes.title: Perverse sheaves and complexes of geometric origin
nodes.statement: For schemes X of finite type over ℂ, the class of simple perverse sheaves of complex vector spaces of geometric origin is the smallest class (a) containing the constant sheaf ℂ on a point and (b) closed under taking the simple constituents of pH^i T(F) for T one of Rf_*, Rf_!, f^*, Rf^! (f a morphism of schemes of finite type over ℂ), and (c) closed under taking the simple constituents of pH^i(A ⊗ B) and pH^i RHom(A, B) for A, B with constituents in the class. A perverse sheaf is semisimple of geometric origin if it is a finite direct sum of simple ones of geometric origin; a complex K ∈ D^b_c(X(ℂ), ℂ) is semisimple of geometric origin if K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(K)[−i] and each pH^i(K) is semisimple of geometric origin.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
The definition is inductive over all schemes of finite type over ℂ; constituents are simple subquotients in the analytic perverse heart.
proofSteps: The class exists as the intersection of all classes with properties (a)–(c).
The full subcategories of D^b_c(X(ℂ), ℂ) of objects whose perverse cohomology constituents are of geometric origin are stable under f_*, f_!, f^*, f^!, ⊗ and RHom by construction (BBD 6.2.4).
acceptance: For j : U ↪ X an open immersion with U smooth connected of dimension d and L a local system with finite monodromy on U, j_!*(L[d]) is semisimple of geometric origin, since L is a direct summand of π_*ℂ for a finite étale cover π.

objects of geometric origin specialise to pure objects over finite fields
IC complexes of local systems of geometric origin on complex varieties

sources.match: BBD define simple perverse sheaves of geometric origin as the smallest class containing ℂ on a point and closed under constituents of perverse cohomology of the four operations and of ⊗, RHom, and define semisimple objects and complexes of geometric origin.

nodes.title: Simple perverse sheaves of geometric origin specialise to pure sheaves over finite fields
nodes.statement: Let F be a simple perverse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaf of geometric origin on X over ℂ (transported from ℂ to ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients by a field isomorphism and EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison). For S = Spec A, A ⊂ ℂ finitely generated over ℤ and large enough, each specialisation equivalence of EDC.7/restricted-constructible-categories sends F to a simple perverse sheaf F_s̄ on X_s̄ satisfying (P): X_s̄ comes by extension of scalars from some X₀ over a finite field 𝔽_q and F_s̄ from a pure perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
The model, the finite field and the pure F₀ are part of the output (a witness), not assumptions; purity is a conclusion.
proofSteps: Simplicity is preserved by the specialisation equivalences (EDC.7/restricted-constructible-categories, perverse t-exactness).

By the inductive definition (EDC.7/geometric-origin-class) it suffices that (P) holds for ℚ̄_ℓ on a point and is stable under the generating operations, which commute with the equivalences after refining and shrinking.

The generating operations preserve mixedness and perverse cohomology of their finite-field models. Their arithmetic simple constituents are pure. A geometric simple constituent need not itself be the pullback of an arithmetic simple object over the original finite field: use the finite-extension/geometrically-simple classification of BBD 5.3.9(ii), recorded in EDC.7/pure-indecomposables, to realize it by a pure model over a finite extension. This is the property used in BBD 6.2.6.
acceptance: For F = ℂ_X[d] with X smooth over ℂ, F₀ can be taken to be ℚ̄_ℓ[d] on a smooth model X₀, pure of weight d.

sources.match: BBD prove that, for S large, the specialisation equivalences send a simple perverse sheaf of geometric origin to a simple perverse sheaf coming from a pure one over a finite field, by stability of property (P) under the generating operations.

nodes.title: The decomposition theorem over ℂ
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over ℂ. If K ∈ D^b_c(X(ℂ), ℂ) is semisimple of geometric origin, then Rf_*K is semisimple of geometric origin: Rf_*K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(Rf_*K)[−i] and each pH^i(Rf_*K) is a finite direct sum of simple perverse sheaves of geometric origin. The same holds with ℂ replaced by ℚ̄_ℓ in the étale topology. In particular, for X smooth (resp. any X and L of geometric origin), Rf_*ℂ_X[dim X] (resp. Rf_*IC_X(L)) decomposes in this way. No ℚ- or ℚ_ℓ-rational descent of the splitting is asserted.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
K semisimple of geometric origin; complex (or ℚ̄_ℓ) coefficients.
proofSteps: Reduce to K = F simple perverse of geometric origin (finite sums and shifts).

Choose S large and specialise (EDC.7/pure-specialization-of-geometric-origin): F_s̄ comes from a pure F₀ on X₀ over 𝔽_q, and f, refined (T, L) on Y and the operation Rf_* are compatible with the equivalences (EDC.7/restricted-constructible-categories).

Over 𝔽̄_q, Rf_*F_s̄ splits as ⊕ pH^i[−i] with semisimple pH^i (EDC.7/decomposition-theorem); transport back through the equivalences to get the statement for Rf_*F; the constituents are of geometric origin by definition (BBD 6.2.7).
acceptance: For the blow-up π of ℂ² at 0, Rπ_*ℂ[2] ≅ ℂ[2] ⊕ ℂ_0 (the complex counterpart of the 𝔽_q example of EDC.7/decomposition-theorem).
For f : X → point with X projective, the theorem gives H*(X, IC_X) as a graded vector space, the content being the existence of the IC formalism rather than splitting.

sources.match: BBD: for proper f, Rf_* of a semisimple complex of geometric origin is semisimple of geometric origin, proved by specialising to a finite field and applying 5.4.5 and 5.3.8.
Survey statement of the decomposition and semisimplicity theorems over ℂ.

nodes.title: Relative hard Lefschetz over ℂ
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a projective morphism of schemes of finite type over ℂ, η the first Chern class of a relatively ample line bundle, and F a semisimple perverse sheaf of geometric origin on X. Then for every i ≥ 0, η^i : pH^{−i}(Rf_*F) → pH^{i}(Rf_*F) is an isomorphism (Tate twists trivialised by the choice of 2πi). For Y a point this is hard Lefschetz in intersection cohomology of complex projective varieties.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
f projective with a chosen relatively ample line bundle; F semisimple of geometric origin.
proofSteps: Write the semisimple F as a finite direct sum of simple geometric-origin constituents. Specialize each constituent to a pure finite-field model, after one common refinement, shrinking and finite residue-field extension that also models f and η. Different constituents may have different weights, so the sum is not asserted to be pure of one weight. Apply the finite-field theorem separately and take the direct sum.
Apply EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem over 𝔽_q and transport back (BBD 6.2.10).
acceptance: For X smooth projective over ℂ and F = ℂ[dim X], Y a point: η^i : H^{n−i}(X, ℂ) ≅ H^{n+i}(X, ℂ), the classical hard Lefschetz theorem.

sources.match: BBD: relative hard Lefschetz for projective f and semisimple perverse sheaves of geometric origin over ℂ, deduced from 6.2.6 and 5.4.10; the case of a point gives hard Lefschetz in intersection cohomology.

nodes.title: Correspondences of schemes and their morphisms
nodes.statement: A correspondence from X₁ to X₂ is a morphism c = (c₁, c₂) : C → X₁ × X₂ of schemes separated of finite type over k. A morphism from c : C → X₁ × X₂ to b : B → Y₁ × Y₂ is a triple [f] = (f₁, f♮, f₂) with b₁f♮ = f₁c₁ and b₂f♮ = f₂c₂. [f] is proper (resp. an open or closed embedding) when f₁, f♮ and f₂ are. A self-correspondence is c : C → X × X; its fixed-point scheme is Fix(c) := C ×_{X×X} X (fibre product with the diagonal Δ), with Δ′ : Fix(c) → C and c′ : Fix(c) → X. A compactification of c is a correspondence c̄ : C̄ → X̄₁ × X̄₂ with C̄, X̄₁ and X̄₂ proper over k with a dominant open embedding [j] : c → c̄; every pair of compactifications of X₁, X₂ extends to one of c.
hypotheses: Schemes separated of finite type over a field k; fibre products are the native scheme fibre products.
proofSteps: Composition of morphisms of correspondences is componentwise; Fix is functorial for morphisms of self-correspondences with f₁ = f₂.
Existence of compactifications: compactify C by Nagata and take the closure of C in C′ × X̄₁ × X̄₂ (Varshavsky 1.1.3).

For the invariance-preserving compactification, use the properness over U to control the closure of the first leg. Blow up the boundary locus to separate the closures that would violate local invariance, and replace the compactification by the proper transform; this is the construction in Varshavsky Lemma 1.5.4, pp.14–15. Nagata compactification and blow-ups are explicit SF.0 requests; IsProper alone supplies neither.
acceptance: The graph-type correspondence (g, id) : X → X × X of an endomorphism g has Fix equal to the fixed-point scheme X^g.
The transpose c^t = (c₂, c₁) has Fix(c^t) ≅ Fix(c).

nodes.title: Cohomological correspondences
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X₁ × X₂ be a correspondence, F₁ ∈ D^b_ctf(X₁, Λ) and F₂ ∈ D^b_ctf(X₂, Λ). A cohomological correspondence lifting c (a c-morphism) from F₁ to F₂ is a morphism u : c₁^*F₁ → c₂^!F₂ in D(C, Λ); equivalently, by the adjunction c₂_! ⊣ c₂^!, a morphism c₂_!c₁^*F₁ → F₂. Hom_c(F₁, F₂) := Hom(c₁^*F₁, c₂^!F₂). Convention: pull back along the first leg and apply the exceptional inverse image along the second; the stage description's c₂^*K → c₁^!K is the same notion with the legs named in the opposite order. For an endomorphism g : X → X, the graph-type correspondence is (g, id) : X → X × X (c₁ = g, c₂ = id), whose c-morphisms are the maps u : g^*F → F.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
proofSteps: The adjunction c₂_! ⊣ c₂^! is EDC.1:adjoint/exceptional-inverse-image; it identifies the two descriptions naturally in F₁, F₂.
For c the identity correspondence of X, Hom_c(F₁, F₂) = Hom(F₁, F₂) (since id^! = id).
acceptance: For c = (g, id) the graph-type correspondence of an endomorphism g, a c-morphism is a map u : g^*F → F; for g the Frobenius of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, the Weil structure Fr^*F ≅ F of a sheaf on X₀ is one.
For X₁ = X₂ = C = Spec k, a c-morphism is a morphism of perfect Λ-complexes F₁ → F₂.

nodes.title: Pushforward of cohomological correspondences and the induced map on compactly supported cohomology
nodes.statement: Let [f] = (f₁, f♮, f₂) : c → b be a morphism of correspondences satisfying one of: (i) the square (c₁, f♮, f₁, b₁) is cartesian; (ii) f₁ and f♮ are proper; (iii) c₁ and b₁ are proper. Then there is a base change morphism BC : b₁^*f₁_! → f♮_!c₁^* (the standard one in (i), (ii); in (iii) adjoint to f₁_! → f₁_!c₁_*c₁^* = b₁_*f♮_!c₁^*), and every c-morphism u : c₂_!c₁^*F₁ → F₂ yields a b-morphism [f]_!(u) : b₂_!b₁^*(f₁_!F₁) → b₂_!f♮_!c₁^*F₁ = f₂_!c₂_!c₁^*F₁ → f₂_!F₂. Pushforwards compose: ([g] ∘ [f])_! = [g]_! ∘ [f]_! when both satisfy the same condition. For c₁ proper, the structure morphism to the trivial correspondence gives RΓ_c(u) : RΓ_c(X₁, F₁) → RΓ_c(X₂, F₂), explicitly RΓ_c(X₁, F₁) → RΓ_c(C, c₁^*F₁) = RΓ_c(X₂, c₂_!c₁^*F₁) → RΓ_c(X₂, F₂), and RΓ_c(u) is unchanged under compactification.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
One of the three admissibility conditions (i)–(iii) for [f]; for RΓ_c(u), c₁ proper.
proofSteps: In case (i) use cartesian base change for compact pushforward Rf_!, which does not require f to be proper. In case (ii) the commutative square need not be cartesian: use the ordinary exchange b₁^*Rf₁_* → Rf♮_*c₁^*, obtained by adjunction, and identify Rf₁_! with Rf₁_* and Rf♮_! with Rf♮_* using their properness. This exchange need not be an isomorphism. In case (iii), with c₁ proper, use the adjoint composite and c₁_! = c₁_* (Varshavsky 1.1.6(a)).
Compatibility with composition reduces to the compatibility of base change morphisms with composition (Varshavsky 1.1.6(b)).
RΓ_c(u) := [π]_!(u) for the structure morphism, which satisfies (iii); independence of compactification by 1.1.6(b) (Varshavsky 1.1.7).
acceptance: For c the graph-type correspondence of g : X → X proper and u : g^*F → F, RΓ_c(u) is the endomorphism of RΓ_c(X, F) induced by g and u (pull back along g, then u).
For the trivial correspondence over Spec k, [π]_! is the identity.

nodes.title: Pullback, open restriction and restriction to invariant closed subsets
nodes.statement: (a) Pullback: if [f] : c → b has its right square cartesian up to nilpotents, or f♮ and f₂ étale, there is BC : c₂_!f♮^* → f₂^*b₂_!, and a b-morphism u gives a c-morphism [f]^*(u) : c₂_!c₁^*(f₁^*F₁) → f₂^*F₂. (b) Open restriction: for a self-correspondence c and open W ⊂ C, U ⊂ X, u restricts to u|_W and to u|_U on c|_U : c₁^{−1}(U) ∩ c₂^{−1}(U) → U × U. (c) A closed Z ⊂ X is c-invariant if c₁(c₂^{−1}(Z)) ⊂ Z set-theoretically, and locally c-invariant if each z ∈ Z has an open neighbourhood U with Z ∩ U c|_U-invariant; for c-invariant Z, c|_Z : c₂^{−1}(Z)_red → Z × Z and u restricts to u|_Z; in general one first restricts to the largest open W(Z) ⊂ C over which Z is invariant. (d) If c₂ is quasi-finite and x is a closed point, Fix(c|_x) is finite and for y ∈ Fix(c|_x) the restriction u_y : F_x → F_x is the summand of (c₂_!c₁^*F)_x → F_x at y; Tr(u_y) is the naive local term.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
proofSteps: (a), (b): base change for cartesian squares up to nilpotents (topological invariance, SF.2) and étale base change (Varshavsky 1.1.8–1.1.9).

(c): the largest open W(Z) is the complement of the closure of c₂^{−1}(Z) ∖ c₁^{−1}(Z) (Varshavsky Lemma 1.5.3(b)); invariance makes the inclusion of c|_Z cartesian up to nilpotents, so (a) applies (1.5.6).
(d): for quasi-finite c₂ the stalk (c₂_!c₁^*F)_x is the direct sum of the stalks of c₁^*F over c₂^{−1}(x) (Varshavsky 1.5.7).
acceptance: For c the graph-type correspondence of an automorphism g with g(Z) = Z, Z is c-invariant and u|_Z is the restricted equivariant structure on F|_Z.
Example 1.5.2 of Varshavsky: a closed point x with c₂^{−1}(x) finite is locally c-invariant.

nodes.title: Composition of cohomological correspondences
nodes.statement: Given cohomological correspondences (c, u) from (X, L) to (Y, M) and (d, v) from (Y, M) to (Z, N), their composite is supported on e : C ×_Y D → X × Z with legs c₁ ∘ pr_C and d₂ ∘ pr_D, and is the composite pr_C^*c₁^*L → pr_C^*c₂^!M → pr_D^!d₁^*M → pr_D^!d₂^!N, where the middle map is the base change pr_C^*c₂^! → pr_D^!d₁^* of the cartesian square (adjoint to the proper/compact base change isomorphism pr_D!pr_C^* ≅ d₁^*c₂!). Composition is associative and unital up to the canonical isomorphisms of fibre products, and is compatible with pushforward to Spec k: for c₁, d₁ proper, RΓ_c of the composite is RΓ_c(v) ∘ RΓ_c(u). Together with external products (X, L) ⊗ (X′, L′) = (X × X′, L ⊠ L′) these form a symmetric monoidal 2-category.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
The base-change maps are those of EDC.1:adjoint/base-change-exchange-maps; external products use finite Tor dimension on both factors.

nodes.title: The trace map of a self-correspondence and its local terms
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, c : C → X × X a self-correspondence and F ∈ D^b_ctf(X, Λ). The trace map Tr_c : Hom(c₂_!c₁^*F, F) → H⁰(Fix(c), K_{Fix(c)}) is H⁰ of the composite RHom(c₁^*F, c₂^!F) ≅ c^!(DF ⊠ F) → c^!Δ_*K_X ≅ Δ′_*c′^!K_X = Δ′_*K_{Fix(c)}, where the first isomorphism is Illusie's Künneth identification, the middle map is induced by DF ⊠ F → Δ_*K_X adjoint to the evaluation DF ⊗ F → K_X, and the last is proper base change for the closed immersion Δ. For an open β ⊂ Fix(c), Tr_β is the restriction to β; if β is proper over k, the local term LT_β(u) ∈ Λ is the image of Tr_β(u) under the integration map π_β! : H⁰(β, K_β) → Λ. For the trivial correspondence over Spec k, Tr is the usual trace of an endomorphism of a perfect complex.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
k separably closed; F of finite Tor dimension, so that biduality and the Künneth identification DF ⊠ F ≅ RHom(pr₁^*F, pr₂^!F) hold (EDC.1:biduality).
proofSteps: First use the requested product-dualizing/Künneth theorem: K_X⊠K_Y ≅ K_(X×Y) and D F⊠G ≅ RHom(pr₁^*F,pr₂^!G) for bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes. Then sheafified adjunction gives RHom(c₁^*F,c₂^!F) ≅ c^!(D F⊠F). EDC.1 relative/geometric duality alone does not state this product factorization; the precise missing supplier is requested from EDC.1:biduality.

The evaluation map and the diagonal adjunction give DF ⊠ F → Δ_*K_X; base change c^!Δ_* ≅ Δ′_*c′^! for the cartesian square defining Fix(c) (EDC.1:adjoint/base-change-exchange-maps), and c′^!K_X = K_{Fix(c)} (Varshavsky 1.2.2(a)).

Local terms by restriction and the proper integration map (Varshavsky 1.2.2(b), (1.3)–(1.4)); the trivial-correspondence case is Varshavsky 1.2.3 and matches the perfect-complex trace of CohomologicalPointCounting TraceFormula Layer 2.
acceptance: For the trivial correspondence pt → pt × pt, Tr(u) = Tr(u | F) for F a perfect Λ-complex (Varshavsky 1.2.3).
For c₂ quasi-finite and an isolated fixed point y over a closed point x with {x} invariant, LT_y(u|_x) = Tr(u_y | F_x), the naive local term (Varshavsky 1.5.7).

nodes.title: Trace maps commute with proper pushforward of correspondences
nodes.statement: Let [f] = (f, f♮, f) be a proper morphism from a self-correspondence c : C → X × X to b : B → Y × Y (the two outer components equal). Then the induced f′ : Fix(c) → Fix(b) is proper and, for every F ∈ D^b_ctf(X, Λ) and u ∈ Hom(c₂_!c₁^*F, F), Tr_b([f]_!(u)) = f′_!(Tr_c(u)) in H⁰(Fix(b), K_{Fix(b)}), where f′_! is the integration map of the proper f′. The correspondences c and b need not be proper.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
[f] proper with equal outer components; k separably closed.
proofSteps: Fix(c) is closed inside C×_B Fix(b): impose equality of the two resulting X-points using the closed diagonal of separated X. The projection C×_B Fix(b)→Fix(b) is proper because f♮ is proper. Hence the induced f′ is proper. It is not simply a base change of f.

For the trace identity use Varshavsky §4.4, pp.36–38. Reduce to the diagonal identity correspondence on X×X; the product-dualizing identification compares the two internal-Hom evaluations. The projection formula and adjunction counits compare this evaluation before and after proper pushforward. The diagrams (4.13)–(4.15) express these compatibilities; applying c^! and proper diagonal base change gives the equality on Fix(b). This uses the coherent six-operation and product-dualizing inputs of EDC.8/trace-map-and-local-terms.
Proposition 1.2.5, through Theorem 4.3.1 and Corollary 4.3.2, then gives the stated identity for proper [f]. Properness of c or b is not required.
acceptance: For b the trivial correspondence and c proper, the statement is the Lefschetz–Verdier formula of EDC.8/lefschetz-verdier-trace-formula.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.2.5, p. 10; Theorem 4.3.1, Corollary 4.3.2 and 4.3.4, pp. 34–36 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: Trace maps commute with proper pushforward of correspondences, without assuming c or b proper.

nodes.title: The Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed and c : C → X × X a self-correspondence proper over k (C and X proper over k). For every F ∈ D^b_ctf(X, Λ) and every c-morphism u : c₂_!c₁^*F → F, Tr(RΓ_c(u) | RΓ_c(X, F)) = Σ_{β ∈ π₀(Fix(c))} LT_β(u). For Λ a field this is Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(H^i_c(u)) = Σ_β LT_β(u). Ordinary Frobenius point counting (Grothendieck–Lefschetz) remains the theorem of CohomologicalPointCounting TraceFormula, and the contracting-boundary refinement is EDC.8/fujiwara-varshavsky-trace-formula.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
c proper over k (the structure morphism [π]_c is proper); for the trace on cohomology, Λ such that RΓ_c(X, F) is perfect.
proofSteps: Apply EDC.8/trace-pushforward-compatibility to the structure morphism [π]_c from c to the trivial correspondence: the left side is Tr([π]_!(u)) (Varshavsky 1.1.7, 1.2.3).
The right side is π_{Fix(c)!}(Tr_c(u)), which splits over the connected components of the proper Fix(c) (Varshavsky Corollary 1.2.6; SGA 5 III 4.7).
acceptance: For X = ⊔_{i∈I} Spec k finite, c the graph-type correspondence of σ : I → I and F = M constant: Tr(RΓ(u)) = Σ_{σ(i)=i} Tr(u_i | M), which is Tau Ceti's LinearMap.trace_pi_of_apply_eq (EDC.8/zero-dimensional-lefschetz-verdier).
For X a smooth proper curve of genus g, c = Δ and F = ℚ_ℓ: χ(X) = 2 − 2g = LT_X(id), the self-intersection of the diagonal.

sources.match: For a correspondence proper over k, the trace of RΓ_c(u) equals the sum of local terms over the connected components of Fix(c).

nodes.title: The Lefschetz–Verdier formula for finite étale schemes and permutation correspondences
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, X = ⊔_{i ∈ I} Spec k for a finite set I, σ : I → I and g : X → X the induced morphism, c = (g, id) its graph-type correspondence, M a finite free Λ-module (Λ a field or ℤ/ℓⁿ) and F the constant sheaf with fibre M, with u : g^*F → F given by endomorphisms u_i : M → M. Then RΓ(X, F) = M^I, RΓ(u) acts by (x_i) ↦ (u_i(x_{σ(i)})), Fix(c) = {i : σ(i) = i}, LT_i(u) = Tr(u_i) and the Lefschetz–Verdier formula reads Tr(RΓ(u)) = Σ_{σ(i)=i} Tr(u_i | M). For field Λ this is Tau Ceti’s LinearMap.trace_pi_of_apply_eq. For Λ=ℤ/ℓⁿ compute the diagonal blocks in a product basis; the cited Tau Ceti theorem is not a ring-coefficient theorem. With M=Λ and u_i=1 it counts fixed points; Mathlib’s Matrix.trace_permutation supplies that special case when σ is a permutation.
hypotheses: X finite étale (a finite disjoint union of copies of Spec k); Λ a field (for the cited linear-algebra lemma) or ℤ/ℓⁿ.
proofSteps: Étale cohomology of a finite disjoint union of separably closed points is the product of fibres in degree 0.
Fix(c) is the reduced finite scheme of fixed indices; at each the local term is naive (EDC.8/correspondence-pullback-and-restriction (d), with c₂ = id quasi-finite).

Over a field use Tau Ceti’s trace_pi_of_apply_eq, whose finite product may be reindexed by an arbitrary self-map σ. For a general coefficient ring and finite free M, choose one basis of M and the induced basis of M^I. The diagonal block at i is u_i if σ(i)=i and zero otherwise; summing matrix diagonal entries proves the identity. Matrix.trace_permutation is a comparison only for an actual permutation σ and rank-one trivial u_i.
acceptance: σ a transposition of I = {1, 2} with u_i = id on M = Λ: trace 0, no fixed points.
σ = id: trace |I| · rank M = Σ_i Tr(id_M).

sources.match: Over a point the trace map is the usual trace, and for quasi-finite c₂ local terms at isolated points are naive traces on stalks.

nodes.title: Additivity of trace maps over an invariant closed subset and its complement
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X × X be a self-correspondence, u : c₂_!c₁^*F → F a c-morphism and Z ⊂ X a closed c-invariant subset with open complement U. Then c₁^{−1}(U) ⊂ c₂^{−1}(U), u|_Z and u|_U extend by zero to c-morphisms [i_Z]_!(u|_Z) and [j_U]_!(u|_U), and Tr_c(u) = Tr_c([i_Z]_!(u|_Z)) + Tr_c([j_U]_!(u|_U)) in H⁰(Fix(c), K_{Fix(c)}). Consequently, for c proper over k, Tr(RΓ_c(u)) = Tr(RΓ_c(u|_Z)) + Tr(RΓ_c(u|_U)).
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
Z closed and c-invariant; k separably closed.
proofSteps: Use the requested filtered derived enhancement and its compatible tensor, internal Hom, six operations and associated-graded functor. For the invariant closed Z and complement U, lift the localization triangle to the two-step filtration with grades i_*F|_Z and j_!F|_U.

Invariance implies RHom(c₂!c₁^*j_!F|_U,i_*F|_Z)=0. Therefore u lifts uniquely through the filtered localization data. This is the filtered lifting calculation in Varshavsky §5.3, pp.42–44, not ordinary triangulated trace additivity without a lift.

The filtered evaluation induces on associated grades the two diagonal evaluations. The trace map is the sum of those grade traces; proper closed-immersion compatibility and open restriction identify them with the closed and open contributions (Proposition 1.5.10).
acceptance: For the graph-type correspondence of an automorphism g of a proper curve and Z = X^g finite, the Lefschetz number splits into the fixed-point contribution and the contribution of U, which has no fixed points.

sources.match: Additivity of trace maps for an invariant closed subset and its open complement, proved through filtered derived categories.

nodes.title: Specialisation of cohomological correspondences over a trait
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, R a discrete valuation ring over k with residue field k (for example k[t]_{(t)} or k[[t]]), D = Spec R with generic point η and closed point s. A separated finite-type X̃ over D lifts X if it comes with ϕ : X̃ → X × D inducing X̃_η ≅ X_η; the specialisation functor is sp_{X̃}(F) := Ψ_{X̃}(ϕ_η^*F_η) : D^b_ctf(X, Λ) → D^b_ctf(X̃_s, Λ), with Ψ the nearby-cycles functor (computed after strict henselisation). A lift f̃ of f gives base-change maps f̃_s^*sp → sp f^*, f̃_s!sp → sp f_!, sp f_* → f̃_s*sp, sp f^! → f̃_s^!sp, isomorphisms for f̃ proper (the ! and * pushforward ones) or smooth (pullback). For a lift c̃ of a correspondence c, every c-morphism u gives a c̃_s-morphism sp_c̃(u) : c̃_s2!c̃_s1^*sp F₁ → sp c₂!c₁^*F₁ → sp F₂. The trace maps commute with specialisation: sp_{Fix(c̃)}(Tr_c(u)) = Tr_{c̃_s}(sp_c̃(u)), where sp_{Fix(c̃)} : H⁰(Fix(c), K) → H⁰(Fix(c̃_s), K) is the induced map; c and c̃ need not be proper. For X̃ = X × D, sp is the identity. In computing Ψ, pass to a strict henselization and a chosen geometric generic point η̄; the functor is i_s^*Rj_η̄* applied to the geometric generic-fibre pullback. Using the ordinary generic point instead would introduce inertia cohomology. The all-finite-type exchange transformations and their adic extension are requested from LPV.0; its existing torsion/quasi-finite functoriality is insufficient by itself.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
R a DVR over k with residue field k; nearby cycles of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0 with torsion coefficients prime to the residue characteristic, extended to adic coefficients.
proofSteps: After strict henselization choose η̄ and use Ψ=i_s^*Rj_η̄* on the geometric generic-fibre complex. Construct the four exchange maps by the corresponding six-operation mates. Proper and smooth exchange are isomorphisms in their stated ranges. LPV.0 supplies torsion geometric nearby cycles; request the all-finite-type transformations and normalized adic-limit compatibilities used here.
For the constant lift, i^*F_D → i^*Rj_*j^*F_D is an isomorphism (Varshavsky 1.3.3(a), Remark 3.2.5).
sp_c̃(u) is the displayed composite (1.3.4); compatibility with trace maps is Varshavsky Proposition 1.3.5, proved with cohomological morphisms in §4 (4.3.4).
acceptance: For the constant lift X × D and c × D, sp_c̃(u) = u and the compatibility is trivial.

nodes.title: Deformation to the normal cone and Verdier’s specialisation isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let Z ⊂ X be a closed subscheme and R as in EDC.8/correspondence-specialization with uniformizer t. The deformation X̃_Z := Spec_{X_D}(O_{X_D}[I_{Z_D}/t]) lifts X, its special fibre is the normal cone N_Z(X) = Spec_Z(⊕_n I_Zⁿ/I_Z^{n+1}), and Z_D ↪ X̃_Z restricts on the special fibre to the zero section Z ⊂ N_Z(X). (a) Verdier: for F ∈ D^b_ctf(X, Λ) the natural map sp_{X̃_Z}(F)|_Z → F|_Z is an isomorphism. (b) Functoriality: for f : X′ → X with f·(I_Z) ⊂ I_{Z′}, f lifts uniquely to f̃ : X̃′_{Z′} → X̃_Z; f̃_s(N_{Z′}(X′)) lies set-theoretically in the zero section iff f·(I_Z)ⁿ ⊂ I_{Z′}^{n+1} for some n; for Z′ = f^{−1}(Z) and f a closed embedding (resp. proper, smooth), so is f̃. (c) A correspondence c lifts to c̃_Z on the deformations, and the deformation of Fix(c) to the normal cone of c′^{−1}(Z) is a closed subscheme of Fix(c̃_Z).
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
Z ⊂ X closed; (a) for all F of finite Tor dimension (in fact for all constructible F).
proofSteps: (b), (c): direct from the definition of the Rees-type algebra O_{X_D}[I_Z/t] (Varshavsky Lemma 1.4.3, Corollary 1.4.5).

For the zero-section isomorphism follow Varshavsky §3, pp.21–25. Localization reduces to vanishing for F|_Z=0. Blow up to make the ideal Cartier, then embed into an affine-space pair with a coordinate hyperplane. The one-dimensional step uses a finite étale trivializing cover, normalization, and cohomological dévissage to obtain generic vanishing. Noether normalization produces a projection finite on the bad-support locus; dimension induction finishes the argument. LPV.0 nearby-cycle exchange and the SF.0 blow-up, Noether-normalization inputs are requested explicitly; SF.0/nagata-normalization-finite supplies finite normalization for the excellent finite-type bases. This is Verdier SP5, not a formal G_m-equivariance calculation.
acceptance: For Z = X the deformation is the constant lift and (a) is the identity.
For X = 𝔸¹, Z = {0}, N_Z(X) = 𝔸¹ and (a) says the nearby cycles of the deformed constant sheaf restrict to F_0 at the zero section.

nodes.title: Contracting correspondences and Frobenius twists
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X × X be a correspondence and Z ⊂ X a closed subscheme. c stabilises Z if c₁·(I_Z) ⊂ c₂·(I_Z)·O_C (scheme-theoretically c₁(c₂^{−1}(Z)) ⊂ Z); c is contracting near Z if it stabilises Z and c₁·(I_Z)ⁿ ⊂ c₂·(I_Z)^{n+1}·O_C for some n ≥ 1; c is contracting near Z in a neighbourhood of fixed points if some open W ⊃ Fix(c) of C has c|_W contracting near Z. Over 𝔽̄_q with c defined over 𝔽_q, the n-th Frobenius twist is c^{(n)} := (Fr_X^n ∘ c₁, c₂) = (c₁ ∘ Fr_C^n, c₂). For f : Y → X and Z ⊂ X a reduced closed subscheme, ram(f, Z) is the least m with (I_{(f^{−1}Z)_red})^m ⊂ I_{f^{−1}Z}; for f quasi-finite, ram(f) := max_x ram(f, x) is finite.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
Schemes noetherian (finite type over k); in the Frobenius statements k = 𝔽̄_q and c is defined over 𝔽_q.
proofSteps: Stabilising Z implies Z_red is c-invariant (Varshavsky Remark 2.1.2(a)); contraction is equivalently the condition that the special fibre of the deformed correspondence c̃_Z maps N_{c^{−1}(Z)}(C) into the zero section of N_Z(X) (Remark 2.1.2(b), via EDC.8/normal-cone-specialization (b)).
ram(f, Z) exists by noetherianity, and is bounded by dim_k k[f^{−1}(x)] for quasi-finite f (Varshavsky 2.2.2).
acceptance: The graph-type correspondence (Fr, id) of the q-Frobenius of X = X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q is contracting near every point x ∈ X₀(𝔽_q): Fr·(I_x) ⊆ I_x^q ⊆ I_x².

For the identity correspondence, contraction fails near a nonempty closed Z whose support |Z| is not open: Nakayama would force |Z| to be open if I_Zⁿ=I_Z^(n+1). This is a condition on support; a nilpotent ideal may make the identity contracting even when Z is a proper closed subscheme.

nodes.title: Local terms of a contracting correspondence are computed on the contracted subscheme
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X × X be contracting near a closed subscheme Z in a neighbourhood of fixed points, and β ⊂ Fix(c) open and connected with c′(β) ∩ Z ≠ ∅. Then (a) β ⊂ c′^{−1}(Z) set-theoretically, so β is an open connected subset of Fix(c|_Z); (b) for every c-morphism u, Tr_β(u) = Tr_β(u|_Z), and if β is proper over k, LT_β(u) = LT_β(u|_Z).
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
k separably closed; contraction near Z on an open neighbourhood of Fix(c).
proofSteps: Replace c by its restriction to a neighbourhood of Fix(c) where it contracts and by C ∖ (Fix(c) ∖ β), so Fix(c) = β.

(a): by EDC.8/normal-cone-specialization (b)–(c) the special fibre of the deformation maps the normal cone of c′^{−1}(Z) in β to the zero section, giving (I_{c′^{−1}Z})ⁿ = (I_{c′^{−1}Z})^{n+1} on β; connectedness and noetherianity force (I_{c′^{−1}Z})ⁿ = 0.

(b): by EDC.8/trace-additivity, Tr_c(u) is the sum of the Z-part (equal to Tr_{c|_Z}(u|_Z) by EDC.8/trace-pushforward-compatibility for the closed embedding) and the U-part; to kill the U-part assume F|_Z = 0 and use EDC.8/correspondence-specialization for c and the deformation c̃_Z: the specialised c-morphism vanishes because the deformed first leg lands in the zero section where sp F = F|_Z = 0 (Verdier, EDC.8/normal-cone-specialization (a)), while sp on Fix is an isomorphism (Varshavsky Theorem 2.1.3).
acceptance: For the graph-type correspondence of Frobenius and Z = {x} a fixed closed point, LT_x(u) is the naive term Tr(u_x | F_x).

sources.locator: Theorem 2.1.3 and its proof, pp. 17–18 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: For a correspondence contracting near Z in a neighbourhood of fixed points, connected components of Fix meeting Z lie in Z and their trace maps and local terms equal those of the restriction to Z.

nodes.title: Frobenius twists are contracting for large powers
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X × X be a correspondence over 𝔽̄_q defined over 𝔽_q. (a) If Z ⊂ X is closed, n satisfies qⁿ > ram(c₂, Z), and Z is c^{(n)}-invariant, then c^{(n)} is contracting near Z. (b) If Z is a closed locally c-invariant subset defined over 𝔽_q, then c^{(n)} is contracting near Z in a neighbourhood of fixed points for every n with qⁿ > ram(c₂, Z). (c) If c₂ is quasi-finite, then for every n with qⁿ > ram(c₂), c^{(n)} is contracting near every closed point in a neighbourhood of fixed points, and Fix(c^{(n)}) is finite.
hypotheses: k = 𝔽̄_q; c defined over 𝔽_q; ram as in EDC.8/contracting-correspondence.
proofSteps: (a): with d = ram(c₂, Z), (c₁^{(n)})·(I_Z) is the qⁿ-th power of an ideal contained in I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)_red}, hence inside I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)_red}^{d+1} ⊂ I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)}, and its d-th power lies in I_{c₂^{−1}(Z)}^{d+1} (Varshavsky Lemma 2.2.3).

(b): a locally c-invariant Z defined over 𝔽_q is locally c^{(n)}-invariant, so it is c^{(n)}|_W-invariant on the open W(Z) ⊃ Fix(c^{(n)}) (EDC.8/correspondence-pullback-and-restriction); apply (a) to c|_W (Varshavsky Corollary 2.2.4(a)).

(c): closed points are locally invariant when c₂ is quasi-finite (Varshavsky Example 1.5.2, Corollary 2.2.4(b)); finiteness of Fix by EDC.8/contracting-local-terms (a) applied at each point (Theorem 2.3.2(a)).
acceptance: For c the identity correspondence of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, c^{(n)} is the graph of Frobenius^n, whose fixed points are X₀(𝔽_{qⁿ}), finite, for every n ≥ 1 (ram = 1).

sources.locator: Lemma 2.2.3, Corollary 2.2.4, pp. 19; Theorem 2.3.2(a), p. 20 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: Twisting a correspondence defined over 𝔽_q by a large power of Frobenius makes it contracting near invariant subsets and near closed points, and makes the fixed-point set finite.

nodes.title: The Fujiwara–Varshavsky trace formula (Deligne’s conjecture)
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X × X be a correspondence over 𝔽̄_q defined over 𝔽_q, and U ⊂ X an open subset defined over 𝔽_q such that the restriction c₁:c₁^{−1}(U)→U is proper, c₂ is quasi-finite over c₂^{−1}(U), and X ∖ U is locally c-invariant. Then there is d ≥ ram(c₂|_{c₂^{−1}(U)}) such that for every F ∈ D^b_ctf(X, Λ) with F|_{X∖U} = 0, every n with qⁿ > d and every c^{(n)}-morphism u : c₂!(c₁^{(n)})^*F → F: Tr(RΓ_c(u)) = Σ_{y ∈ Fix(c^{(n)}) ∩ c₂^{−1}(U)} Tr(u_y | F_{c₂(y)}), a finite sum of naive local terms. If X and C are proper, d := max{ram(c₂|_{c₂^{−1}(U)}), ram(c₂, X ∖ U)} works. For F with a Weil structure ψ : Fr^*F → F and a c-morphism u, u^{(n)} := u ∘ ψⁿ is a c^{(n)}-morphism, and for U = X this is Deligne's conjecture proved by Fujiwara.
hypotheses: k = 𝔽̄_q; c and U defined over 𝔽_q; the properness/quasi-finiteness over U and local invariance of X ∖ U; Λ and D^b_ctf as in EDC.8/scheme-correspondence's setting; RΓ_c(u) as in Varshavsky 2.3.1 (defined using c₁ proper over U and F|_{X∖U} = 0).
proofSteps: Restrict to c₁⁻¹U and use properness of c₁:c₁⁻¹U→U to construct RΓ_c(u); the assumption F|_(X∖U)=0 identifies RΓ_c(U,F|_U) with RΓ_c(X,F). This is Varshavsky 2.3.1.

Reduce (b) to (c): restrict to c₁^{−1}(U), compactify so that X̄ ∖ U stays locally invariant (Varshavsky Lemma 1.5.4), and extend u by zero; traces are unchanged (EDC.8/cohomological-correspondence-pushforward).

(c): by EDC.8/lefschetz-verdier-trace-formula, Tr(RΓ_c(u)) = Σ_β LT_β(u). Components with c₂(β) ⊂ X ∖ U: c^{(n)} contracts near X ∖ U (EDC.8/frobenius-twist-contracting (b)), so LT_β(u) = LT_β(u|_{X∖U}) = 0 as F|_{X∖U} = 0 (EDC.8/contracting-local-terms).

Components meeting c₂^{−1}(U) are points y (EDC.8/frobenius-twist-contracting (c)), c^{(n)} contracts near c₂(y), and LT_y(u) = LT_y(u|_x) = Tr(u_y) (EDC.8/contracting-local-terms and the naive term of EDC.8/correspondence-pullback-and-restriction (d)) (Varshavsky Theorem 2.3.2, Remark 2.3.3).
acceptance: For c the identity correspondence of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q with X₀ proper, U = X and u^{(n)} = ψⁿ the Weil structure: the formula is the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula Tr(Frⁿ | RΓ(X, F)) = Σ_{x ∈ X₀(𝔽_{qⁿ})} Tr(Frⁿ_x | F_x), the theorem of CohomologicalPointCounting TraceFormula Layer 11, here recovered for all n ≥ 1 (ram = 1).

For a Hecke correspondence of a compactified modular curve with U the open modular curve, the formula computes Tr(Frobⁿ ∘ T | H_c) by fixed points in U for n large, the input consumed by EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.5 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.1a.

sources.match: Varshavsky's generalisation of Fujiwara's theorem: for qⁿ large, the trace of a Frobenius-twisted correspondence on compactly supported cohomology is the sum of naive local terms over fixed points in U; for U = X it is Deligne's conjecture proved by Fujiwara.

nodes.title: Local terms at tame and semisimple isolated fixed points
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed and X separated of finite type over k. (a) If f:X→X fixes x and N_x(f) has no nonzero fixed points, then x is isolated and LT_x(u)=Tr(u_x|F_x) for any u:f*F→F with F constructible of finite Tor dimension. (b) If X is smooth at an isolated fixed point x of a semisimple element g of a linear algebraic group acting on X, the normal-cone hypothesis holds and the same equality follows. (c) For an automorphism g of finite order invertible in k, the equality holds at every isolated fixed point, including singular ones, by applying the trace comparison to the full fixed subscheme Z=Fix(g). If X is proper and X^g has finite support, its global trace is the sum of their stalk traces. The cone of the reduced point can have nonzero fixed points even in (c); it is not an asserted intermediate result. The perfect-scheme transport is a separate Part II target. (d) More generally, if g is a semisimple element of a linear algebraic group acting on X and x is isolated in the fixed support, then LT_x(u)=Tr(u_x), even for singular nonnormal X and infinite-order g: apply the full Artin fixed-subscheme theorem below. For proper X with finite fixed support the global trace is the sum of these stalk traces.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
k algebraically closed; for (c), g^m = id as k-scheme automorphisms with m invertible in k, so that ⟨g⟩ is a finite diagonalizable group of order prime to p.

Only (b) requires smoothness at x. In (c) use the full fixed subscheme, not the reduced point. The smooth fixed-locus/tangent identification for the diagonalizable closure of ⟨g⟩ is an explicit SF.0 request; no general fixed-scheme/normal-cone comparison is assumed.
proofSteps: (a) Apply the proper-component part of normal-cone-trace-comparison with Z={x}; its restricted trace is the stalk trace.

(b) For the diagonalizable closure D of ⟨g⟩, the fixed locus of smooth X is smooth at x and its tangent space is (T_xX)^D. An isolated fixed point has zero fixed tangent space. Since N_xX=T_xX when X is smooth, the cone condition follows. This uses the precise smooth fixed-locus input requested from SF.0, not the false general Lemma 5.1.

(c) Use the tame-fixed-subscheme-normal-cone theorem with the full scheme Z=Fix(g), which gives NoAlmostTubularFixed without smoothness. Apply normal-cone-trace-comparison to Z. An isolated component β of Z has finite nonreduced support, is proper over k, and has the same étale site as its reduced point. The restricted graph is the identity correspondence because g|Z=id. Thus its local term is the stalk trace. For the global statement sum these terms in the proper Lefschetz–Verdier formula.

For arbitrary semisimple g, use EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8/semisimple-isolated-fixed-subscheme-normal-cone: the finite-jet rational diagonalizable action has no invariant conormal character, so the cone along the full Artin fixed component satisfies Theorem 4.10(b). This supplies the previously missing singular application without an equivariant affine neighbourhood.
acceptance: For the involution x ↦ −x of ℙ¹ (p ≠ 2) with F = Λ, u = id: fixed points 0 and ∞, naive terms 1 + 1 = 2 = Tr(g^* | H⁰ ⊕ H²) = 1 + 1.

The finite-order hypothesis matters: for translation by 1 on 𝔸¹ ⊂ ℙ¹ in characteristic p (order p, not prime to p), the unique fixed point ∞ has naive term 1 while Tr(g^* | H*(ℙ¹)) = 2, so the local term at ∞ is 2, not naive.

On Spec k[x,y,z]/(x³+yz) with g=(x,−y,−z), char k≠2, the reduced-origin cone has a fixed x-line. This disproves the reduced-point cone implication, but the full fixed scheme is Spec k[x]/(x³) and its conormal has eigenvalue −1. The full-fixed-subscheme theorem proves LT_0(u)=Tr(u_0).

sources.locator: Theorem 4.10 and Corollary 4.11, p. 10; Lemma 5.1–Corollary 5.6, pp. 10–11 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: Theorem 4.10(b) and Corollary 4.11 prove (a). The general singular implications of Lemma 5.1 and Corollaries 5.4/5.6 fail as recorded in sourceIssues. The smooth specialization uses the smooth fixed-locus tangent theorem, and the finite-order conclusion is repaired via the full-fixed-subscheme cone argument.

sources.locator: Proposition 5.6.2 and its proof, p. 61 (arXiv v4)
sources.match: HKW Proposition 5.6.2 has a finite prime-to-p order hypothesis and an isolated fixed point. Its finite-type input is repaired here using the full fixed subscheme, independently of the cited false cone implication. Its perfect-scheme reduction still needs compatible operations and trace transport in the proposed Part II. It is not a claim about trace classes on a general positive-dimensional closed subscheme.
The version of record retains the false general fixed-cone assertions despite adding reducedness of D; both counterexamples satisfy that hypothesis.

nodes.title: Characteristic polynomials of the two sides of a similitude are reciprocal
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, V and W vector spaces of the same finite dimension b over F, ⟨·,·⟩ : V × W → F a perfect pairing, c ∈ F^×, and φ ∈ GL(V), ψ ∈ GL(W) with ⟨φv, ψw⟩ = c⟨v, w⟩ for all v, w. Then, under W ≅ V^∨ given by the pairing, ψ = c·(φ^∨)^{−1}; consequently det(ψ) = c^b det(φ)^{−1} and, in F[t], det(1 − tψ | W) = det(φ)^{−1}·det(φ − ct | V); equivalently, in F(t), det(1 − tψ | W) = (−ct)^b·det(φ)^{−1}·det(1 − (ct)^{−1}φ | V). Over an algebraic closure, the eigenvalues of ψ with algebraic multiplicity are the c/α for α the eigenvalues of φ. No semisimplicity of φ or ψ is assumed.
hypotheses: F any field; ⟨·,·⟩ perfect; φ, ψ invertible; similitude factor c ∈ F^× (the same on both sides).
proofSteps: ⟨v, ψw⟩ = c⟨φ^{−1}v, w⟩, so the functional ⟨·, ψw⟩ equals c·⟨·, w⟩ ∘ φ^{−1}; i.e. ψ corresponds to c·(φ^{−1})^∨ = c·(φ^∨)^{−1}.
det(1 − tψ) = det(1 − tc·(φ^∨)^{−1}) = det(1 − tc·φ^{−1}) (transpose invariance, mathlib:Matrix.charpoly_transpose / mathlib:LinearMap.det_dualMap) = det(φ)^{−1} det(φ − ct).

Taking t = 0 in det(ψ − x) form, or comparing constant terms, gives det ψ = c^b det(φ)^{−1}; the eigenvalue statement is the root statement for det(φ − ct) (compare mathlib:Matrix.charpoly_inv for c = 1).
acceptance: b = 1, V = W = F with ⟨v, w⟩ = vw, φ = α, ψ = c/α: det(1 − tψ) = 1 − (c/α)t and det(φ)^{−1}det(φ − ct) = (α − ct)/α.
A unipotent φ (Jordan block, α = 1) with c = q gives ψ with the single eigenvalue q of the same algebraic multiplicity, without diagonalisability.

sources.match: Poincaré duality is a perfect Frobenius-compatible pairing H^i × H^{2n−i} → ℚ_ℓ(−n), so the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^{2n−i} are the qⁿ/α for α those on H^i; the linear-algebra step is the similitude identity stated here.

nodes.title: The determinant of a similitude of a symmetric or alternating form
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, V of finite dimension b with a perfect bilinear form ⟨·,·⟩ which is symmetric (ε = +1) or alternating (ε = −1), c ∈ F^×, and φ ∈ GL(V) with ⟨φv, φw⟩ = c⟨v, w⟩. Fix s ∈ F̄ with s² = c and let m_± be the algebraic multiplicity of ±s as an eigenvalue of φ (the dimension of the generalized eigenspace over F̄). Then: (a) generalized eigenspaces V_α, V_β (α, β ∈ F̄) are orthogonal unless αβ = c, and V_α, V_{c/α} have equal dimension; (b) det(φ)² = c^b; (c) if ε = −1, then b, m_+ and m_− are even and det(φ) = c^{b/2}; (d) if ε = +1, then m_+ + m_− ≡ b (mod 2) and det(φ) = (−1)^{m_−} s^b, thus det(φ)=(−1)^{b−m_+}s^b as well. If b is even, s^b=c^{b/2}, and only then this simplifies to det(φ)=(−1)^{m_−}c^{b/2}. In odd rank retain s^b, even when s lies in F. For c=q^d with d even use s=q^{d/2}, so s^b=q^{(d/2)·b}, with no parity assumption on b.
hypotheses: char F ≠ 2; form perfect and ε-symmetric; φ a similitude with factor c; no semisimplicity of φ.
proofSteps: Extend scalars to an algebraic closure. Mathlib’s iSup_maxGenEigenspace_eq_top supplies the spanning primary spaces, and finrank_maxGenEigenspace_eq identifies their dimensions with charpoly.rootMultiplicity. Distinct primary spaces are independent by the coprime-polynomial kernel decomposition; the subsequent form argument uses these generalized spaces, not ordinary eigenspaces.

(a): write φ = α + N on V_α and φ = β + N′ on V_β with N, N′ nilpotent; then (c − αβ)⟨v, w⟩ = α⟨v, N′w⟩ + β⟨Nv, w⟩ + ⟨Nv, N′w⟩, and induction on the nilpotency orders gives ⟨v, w⟩ = 0 when αβ ≠ c; perfectness then pairs V_α perfectly with V_{c/α}.
(b) is EDC.8/similitude-charpoly-reciprocity with W = V, ψ = φ: det φ = c^b det(φ)^{−1}.
Eigenvalues α ≠ ±s come in pairs {α, c/α} of equal multiplicity, each pair contributing c^{dim V_α}; so det φ = c^{(b − m_+ − m_−)/2} s^{m_+} (−s)^{m_−} = (−1)^{m_−} s^b, and b − m_+ − m_− is even.

(c): V_s and V_{−s} are self-paired, so the alternating form restricts to perfect alternating forms on them: m_± even and det φ = s^b = c^{b/2} (b even for an alternating perfect form; Tau Ceti's rank-two case is LinearMap.det_eq_of_compl₁₂_self_eq_smul). Even rank of a perfect alternating space follows by choosing x,y with nonzero pairing, splitting off their nondegenerate two-dimensional plane and inducting on its orthogonal complement. Apply this to V, V_s and V_(−s); this supplies the evenness rather than presuming it from the rank-two determinant citation.
acceptance: Rank-two alternating case: det φ = c, matching tauceti:LinearMap.det_eq_of_compl₁₂_self_eq_smul.
Symmetric rank one with ⟨x, y⟩ = xy and φ = −s (c = s²): m_− = 1 and det φ = −s, so the sign is not determined by the form alone.
Isometries (c = 1): det(φ)² = 1, matching tauceti:TauCeti.BilinForm.IsIsometry.det_sq_mul_det_toMatrix_self.

sources.match: For n odd the middle form is alternating so b_n is even; for n even the sign of the functional equation is (−1)^N with N the dimension of the generalized eigenspace of q^{n/2}.
The sign of the functional equation is + if d is odd or q^{d/2} occurs an even number of times as an eigenvalue on H^d, and − otherwise.

nodes.title: Graded Frobenius duality data of weight (2d, q^d)
nodes.statement: Fix a field E of characteristic 0, an integer d ≥ 0 and q ∈ E^×. A graded Frobenius duality datum consists of finite-dimensional E-vector spaces H^i (0 ≤ i ≤ 2d; zero otherwise), automorphisms F_i ∈ GL(H^i), and perfect pairings ⟨·,·⟩_i : H^i × H^{2d−i} → E such that ⟨F_i x, F_{2d−i} y⟩_i = q^d ⟨x, y⟩_i and ⟨x, y⟩_i = (−1)^i ⟨y, x⟩_{2d−i} (the Koszul sign (−1)^{i(2d−i)} = (−1)^i of graded commutativity). Its Betti numbers are b_i := dim H^i, its Euler characteristic χ := Σ (−1)^i b_i, its polynomials P_i(t) := det(1 − tF_i | H^i) and its determinant Δ := ∏_i det(F_i)^{(−1)^i} ∈ E^×. The middle form ⟨·,·⟩_d is (−1)^d-symmetric.
hypotheses: E of characteristic 0 (so ℚ_ℓ with ℓ = 2 is allowed, and alternating and symmetric are distinct); pairings perfect; F acts by a similitude of factor q^d; no semisimplicity of F.
proofSteps: The data are linear algebra; the main instance is built from EDC.2's Poincaré duality: for X₀ smooth proper of pure dimension d over 𝔽_q and ℓ ∤ q, H^i := H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ), F_i := geometric Frobenius, ⟨x, y⟩_i := Tr(x ∪ y) with the trace H^{2d}(X, ℚ_ℓ) → ℚ_ℓ(−d) composed with the identification of ℚ_ℓ(−d) on which F acts by q^d (EDC.2:pairings/cup-product-trace-pairing, EDC.2:pairings/galois-frobenius-equivariance, EDC.2:pairings/adic-and-rational-poincare-duality).
Graded commutativity of cup product gives the Koszul sign; equivariance of the trace under Frobenius gives the similitude factor q^d (Weil I (2.5)).

A second instance: X₀ proper of pure dimension d whose dualizing complex has a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism a^!ℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(d)[2d] (a rational homology manifold), with the pairing from EDC.1:biduality/relative-and-geometric-duality; this is the datum WeilConjectures:WC.6/homology-manifold-weil-assembly needs.
acceptance: ℙ¹ over 𝔽_q: H⁰ = E with F = 1, H² = E with F = q, ⟨1, 1⟩ = 1; d = 1, χ = 2, Δ = q.
A smooth projective curve of genus g: H¹ of dimension 2g with the alternating cup-product form and F a symplectic similitude of factor q.

uses.how: the graded duality of smooth proper varieties gives reciprocal polynomials and Δ² = q^{dχ}
the middle form is alternating for d odd, so b_d is even
proper rational homology manifolds give the same datum without smoothness or projectivity
dual isotypic pieces paired by a Frobenius similitude

api.name: TauCeti.GradedFrobeniusDuality
api.statement: Data: d≥0,q∈E×,finite-dimensional H^i for i∈ℤ with H^i=0 outside 0≤i≤2d,automorphisms F_i,perfect pairings H^i×H^(2d−i)→E and the similitude/Koszul laws. An ℕ-indexed implementation includes explicit vanishing above 2d and uses pairs i,j with i+j=2d, avoiding unrestricted subtraction on ℕ.

sources.match: Poincaré duality for smooth proper varieties is a perfect Frobenius-compatible pairing with values in ℚ_ℓ(−n), graded commutative, alternating in the middle degree for n odd.

nodes.title: Reciprocity of Frobenius polynomials and the determinant relation
nodes.statement: For a graded Frobenius duality datum (EDC.8/graded-frobenius-duality-datum) of weight (2d, q^d): (a) b_i = b_{2d−i}; (b) for 0 ≤ i ≤ 2d, P_{2d−i}(t)·det(F_i) = (−q^d t)^{b_i}·P_i(1/(q^d t)) as an identity in E(t), and the eigenvalues of F_{2d−i} with algebraic multiplicity are the q^d/α for α those of F_i; (c) det(F_i)·det(F_{2d−i}) = q^{d b_i}; (d) if d is odd, b_d is even and det(F_d) = q^{d b_d/2}; if d is even, det(F_d) = (−1)^{m_−} q^{(d/2)·b_d} = (−1)^{b_d − m_+} q^{(d/2)·b_d}, where m_± is the algebraic multiplicity of ±q^{d/2} as an eigenvalue of F_d; (e) Δ² = q^{dχ}, and dχ is even. These are statements about the actual finite-dimensional spaces; no semisimplicity of Frobenius is assumed, and no zeta function is defined here (WeilConjectures:WC.2 assembles the signed functional equation from them). For X₀ smooth proper over 𝔽_q of pure dimension d and E = ℚ_ℓ (ℓ ∤ q, ℓ = 2 allowed) these apply to H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ) with geometric Frobenius, and likewise for proper rational homology manifolds.
hypotheses: A graded Frobenius duality datum over a field of characteristic 0; for the geometric instances, the hypotheses of EDC.2:pairings (smooth proper) or a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism a^!ℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(d)[2d] (homology manifold).
For odd d the exponent d·b_d/2 is an integer because b_d is even. For even d use (d/2)·b_d; writing d·(b_d/2) would be incorrect when b_d is odd.
proofSteps: (a): the pairing H^i × H^{2d−i} → E is perfect.

(b), (c): apply EDC.8/similitude-charpoly-reciprocity to V = H^i, W = H^{2d−i}, φ = F_i, ψ = F_{2d−i}, c = q^d: det(1 − tF_{2d−i}) = det(F_i)^{−1} det(F_i − q^d t), and det(F_i − q^d t) = (−q^d t)^{b_i} det(1 − (q^d t)^{−1}F_i).
(d): the middle form is (−1)^d-symmetric (Koszul sign); apply EDC.8/form-similitude-determinant with c = q^d and s = q^{d/2} when d is even.

(e): pairing i with 2d − i (same parity), Δ² = ∏_i (det F_i · det F_{2d−i})^{(−1)^i} = ∏_i q^{d b_i (−1)^i} = q^{dχ}; dχ is even because d even, or d odd and χ ≡ b_d ≡ 0 mod 2 after pairing the other degrees.
acceptance: ℙ¹: P₂(t)·det(F₀) = 1 − qt = (−qt)·(1 − 1/(qt)) = (−qt)·P₀(1/(qt)); Δ = q, χ = 2, Δ² = q².
A curve of genus g: det(F₁) = q^g (alternating middle form), Δ = 1 · q^{−g} · q = q^{1−g}, χ = 2 − 2g and Δ² = q^{2−2g} = q^{dχ}.

A smooth quadric surface over 𝔽_q (d = 2) whose two rulings are swapped by Frobenius: F on H² = ℚ_ℓ(−1)² has eigenvalues q and −q, m_− = 1, so det(F₂) = −q², the sign that the split quadric (eigenvalue q twice) does not have.

sources.match: Eigenvalues on H^{2n−i} are qⁿ/α; the functional equation Z(X₀, t) = ε q^{−nχ/2} t^{−χ} Z(X₀, q^{−n}t^{−1}) with ε = 1 for n odd and (−1)^N for n even, N the multiplicity of q^{n/2}.
The sign of the functional equation from the multiplicity of q^{d/2} on H^d.

nodes.title: Fixed-point conditions in a punctured tubular neighbourhood
nodes.statement: For a self-correspondence c:C→X×X and closed Z⊂X, let N_Z(c):N_(c⁻¹(Z×Z))C→N_ZX×N_ZX be the induced conical correspondence and let V=Fix(c|Z) be its vertex. Define NoTubularFixed(c,Z) by |Fix(N_Z(c))|∖|V|=∅. Define NoAlmostTubularFixed(c,Z) by NoTubularFixed together with finiteness of {t∈k : |Fix((t·N_Z(c)₁,N_Z(c)₂))|∖|V|≠∅}. In the comparison theorem Z is schematically c-invariant: c₂⁻¹Z⊆c₁⁻¹Z, equivalently c₂⁻¹Z=c⁻¹(Z×Z). This is stronger than invariance only of underlying sets.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
Use scheme inverse images and relative normal cones; the two fixed-point predicates compare underlying sets. Scalar t=0 is included.
proofSteps: Functoriality of relative normal cones defines both legs and their common vertex. The scalar action on the first leg defines the family.
The inclusion N_(Fix(c|Z))Fix(c)↪Fix(N_Z(c)) and Nakayama show that NoTubularFixed makes Fix(c|Z) an open and closed part of Fix(c) after reduction (Lemma 4.8).

For a contracting correspondence restricted to a neighbourhood of its fixed points, the first cone leg has set-theoretic image in the vertex. Every scalar then has empty punctured fixed locus (Lemma 4.7).
acceptance: For graph x↦λx on 𝔸¹, Z={0}, λ∈k×∖{1}, NoTubularFixed holds and the bad-scalar set is {λ⁻¹}.
For the identity of 𝔸¹ at Z={0}, NoTubularFixed fails.

sources.match: Defines the two punctured-cone conditions and their relation to contraction and isolation.
