nodes.title: Square improvement on the product of a curve
nodes.statement: For a smooth finite-field curve U₀ and lisse punctually ι-pure weight-zero ℱ₀, every eigenvalue α of H¹_c(U,ℱ) satisfies w_ι(α)≤1+2^(−k), for every integer k≥0. The step k→k+1 is proved on a pencil in the compactified surface U₀×U₀ and uses the three coefficient-specific vanishing-cycle cases; it is not a direct application of the general direct-image theorem.
proofSteps: The initial bound supplies k=0. A finite surjective cover by a smooth curve makes boundary monodromy tame unipotent; pullback on compact-support cohomology is injective via the trace map over ℚ_ℓ. Finite base extension arranges general position and rational exceptional values; descend the result.

Put ℋ=ℱ⊠ℱ on the open product surface and blow up the pencil axis. Leray in total degree two has terms H²(ℙ¹,R⁰f_!ℋ), H¹(ℙ¹,R¹f_!ℋ), H⁰(ℙ¹,R²f_!ℋ). Blowup pullback is injective and Künneth embeds H¹_c(U,ℱ)⊗H¹_c(U,ℱ) in the abutment.

The real envelope ℋ⊕ℋ∨ is pure of weight zero and real. Reality of fibre cohomological polynomials makes the lisse R¹ a direct summand of an ι-real sheaf; generalized majoration supplies its finite pure-constituent filtration. The strict H¹ bound gives all constituent weights <2.

The five-term specialization sequence from Φ^a=0 for a≠1 shows R¹ has no sections supported at exceptional values. Intersect its lisse pure filtration with its injection into j_*j*R¹. Every nonconstant graded constituent has a nonzero exceptional quotient somewhere, since otherwise it extends lisse over simply connected ℙ¹ and is geometrically constant.

The local monodromy theorem and the three Φ¹ computations make each such nonconstant constituent weight an integer; hence its weight is ≤1. Apply the inductive bound to its H¹. Geometrically constant constituents contribute H¹=0. This bounds the middle Leray term by 2+2^(−k); invariant/coinvariant descriptions bound the two outer terms by 2.
The finite Leray filtration transfers the bound to α². Divide by two to get w_ι(α)≤1+2^(−k−1), with no degeneration or semisimplicity assumption.
acceptance: The integer-weight step is essential: a real weight <2 need not be ≤1.
The empty vanishing-cycle case yields a constant constituent and zero H¹, not a failed irreducibility argument.
No theorem from DWP.7 is used in the proof of its own curve input.

nodes.title: Deligne's fundamental theorem: R^i f_! of a mixed sheaf of weights ≤ n has weights ≤ n + i
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a separated morphism of schemes of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] and ℱ a sheaf on X, mixed of weights ≤ n. Then for every i the sheaf R^i f_!ℱ on Y is mixed of weights ≤ n + i. In particular, for X₀ of finite type over 𝔽_q, Y₀ = Spec 𝔽_q and ℱ₀ mixed of weights ≤ n (a Weil sheaf being allowed), every eigenvalue α of the geometric Frobenius F on H^i_c(X, ℱ) is an algebraic number for which there is an integer w ≤ n + i with |σ(α)| = q^{w/2} for every field embedding σ : ℚ(α) → ℂ.
hypotheses: f separated of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] (both characteristic p and mixed characteristic bases)
ℱ mixed: integer weights in the all-embeddings sense
Only an upper bound: no lower bound and no purity is asserted

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: By EDC.7/weight-spreading-out-to-a-tame-relative-curve it suffices to treat the tame smooth projective relative curve, which is EDC.7/weight-purity-of-the-relative-curve-case.

The finite-field case is the case Y = Spec 𝔽_q; H^i_c(X, ℱ) is the geometric stalk of R^i f_!ℱ, with F acting as the geometric Frobenius of the closed point (Weil-sheaf variant: Weil II 1.1.10–1.1.14, EDC.7/weight-weil-sheaf).
A sheaf on Spec 𝔽_q mixed of weights ≤ n + i is a Frobenius module whose eigenvalues are Weil q-numbers of integer weights ≤ n + i (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number).
acceptance: Acceptance: X₀ = 𝔾_m, ℱ₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ: weights 0 on H¹_c and 2 on H²_c, both ≤ i.
Acceptance: X₀ = Spec 𝔽_q ⊔ Spec 𝔽_q, ℱ₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ(1): H⁰_c = ℚ̄_ℓ(1)² has weight −2 ≤ −2 + 0.
Acceptance (relative, mixed characteristic): for f : 𝔸¹_{ℤ[1/ℓ]} → Spec ℤ[1/ℓ] and ℱ = ℚ̄_ℓ, R²f_!ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) is pure of weight 2 at every closed point 𝔽_p, p ≠ ℓ.
Non-example: the theorem gives no lower bound: H¹_c(𝔾_m) has weight 0 < 1.

nodes.title: The direct-image theorem for ι-mixed sheaves with real weights
nodes.statement: Fix a field isomorphism ι : ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ and β ∈ ℝ. Let f : X → Y be a separated morphism of schemes of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] and ℱ an ι-mixed sheaf on X with punctual ι-weights ≤ β. Then for every i, R^i f_!ℱ is ι-mixed, and every punctual ι-weight of R^i f_!ℱ is ≤ β + i and congruent modulo ℤ to one of the punctual ι-weights of ℱ. Over 𝔽_q (Weil sheaves allowed), every eigenvalue of F on H^i_c(X, ℱ) has ι-weight ≤ β + i in such a class. No algebraicity, no integrality and no bound at another embedding follows from this statement.
hypotheses: One fixed ι; real weights
The integrality argument of Weil II 3.3.2 does not apply to ι-mixed sheaves

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Rerun EDC.7/weight-spreading-out-to-a-tame-relative-curve and EDC.7/weight-purity-of-the-relative-curve-case with ι-weights: the dévissages hold verbatim for ι-mixed sheaves, and EDC.7/weight-sharp-curve-purity and EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries supply the fixed-ι curve and local statements.

Weights mod ℤ: in the reduced situation the weights of R^q f̄_*(j_*ℱ) are β + q and those of Gr^M_k are β + k, all in β + ℤ; the dévissages only take extensions and subquotients, so every weight produced lies in the class mod ℤ of a weight of the input.
acceptance: Acceptance: on Spec 𝔽_q the rank-one Weil sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ^{(b)} with b = q^{1/3} (a chosen cube root) is ι-pure of weight 2/3 for every ι; for X₀ = 𝔾_m and ℱ₀ the pullback, H¹_c and H²_c have ι-weights 2/3 and 8/3, both ≡ 2/3 mod ℤ.
Non-example: the conclusion does not say that eigenvalues are algebraic: a transcendental b with |ιb| = 1 gives an ι-pure sheaf of weight 0 whose H⁰ has a transcendental eigenvalue.

nodes.title: The direct-image theorem for a tame smooth projective relative curve
nodes.statement: In the reduced situation of EDC.7/weight-spreading-out-to-a-tame-relative-curve (f̄ : X̄ → Y projective and smooth of pure relative dimension 1 over an integral regular Y of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ], j : X = X̄ − D → X̄ with i : D → X̄ the inclusion of a divisor finite étale over Y, and ℱ lisse on X, punctually pure of weight n and tamely ramified along D), R^i f_!ℱ is mixed of weights ≤ n + i for every i. More precisely Rf_!ℱ = Rf̄_*(j_!ℱ); R^i f̄_*(j_*ℱ) is punctually pure of weight n + i; and i*j_*ℱ carries the filtration induced by the local monodromy filtration M along D, with Gr^M_k(i*j_*ℱ) zero for k > 0 and punctually pure of weight n + k on D for k ≤ 0. The ι-version holds with n replaced by β ∈ ℝ.
hypotheses: f̄ projective smooth of relative dimension 1; D finite étale over Y; ℱ tamely ramified along D
Used for every isomorphism ι : ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ to obtain integer weights

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Proper base change and tameness: because D is finite étale over Y and ℱ is tame along D, the formation of j_*ℱ, i*j_*ℱ and the local monodromy filtration M commutes with passage to the fibres X̄_y, y ∈ |Y| (Weil II 1.8.6–1.8.8, supplied by EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries; base change of j_* for tame sheaves along a relative divisor with normal crossings, EDC.0/SF.2). So R^i f̄_*(j_*ℱ) and i*j_*ℱ may be computed fibrewise.

On each fibre, a smooth projective curve over the finite field k(y) with a lisse sheaf punctually ι-pure of weight n on the complement of D_y: EDC.7/weight-sharp-curve-purity (Weil II 3.2.3), applied for every ι, gives that H^i(X̄_ȳ, j_*ℱ) is punctually pure of weight n + i.

EDC.7/weight-local-monodromy-purity and EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries (Weil II 1.8.4 with 1.8.8, for every ι) gives that Gr^M_k(i*j_*ℱ) vanishes for k > 0 and is punctually pure of weight n + k ≤ n on D.

Apply R f̄_* to 0 → j_!ℱ → j_*ℱ → i_*i*j_*ℱ → 0. Since f̄∘i : D → Y is finite, dévissage (f) shows R^q(f̄ i)_*(i*j_*ℱ) vanishes for q ≠ 0 and R⁰ is mixed of weights ≤ n. The long exact sequence then gives R^q f̄_*(j_!ℱ) as an extension of a subsheaf of R^q f̄_*(j_*ℱ) (weight n + q) by a quotient of R^{q−1}(f̄ i)_*(...) (weights ≤ n ≤ n + q), which is mixed of weights ≤ n + q by dévissage (a).
acceptance: Acceptance: for Y = Spec 𝔽_q, X̄ = ℙ¹, D = {0, ∞} and ℱ = ℚ̄_ℓ: H¹_c(𝔾_m) = ℚ̄_ℓ (weight 0 ≤ 1), H²_c(𝔾_m) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) (weight 2): the bound is an upper bound, attained only in degree 2.
Acceptance: for an elliptic curve E over 𝔽_q minus its origin and ℱ = ℚ̄_ℓ: H¹_c = H¹(E) is pure of weight 1.
Non-example: without tameness along D the formation of j_*ℱ need not commute with base change to the fibres, and the fibrewise computation is not available.

nodes.title: Reduction of the direct-image theorem to a tame smooth projective relative curve
nodes.statement: Assume Theorem 3.3.1 holds for every quadruple (f̄, D, ℱ, Y) of the following kind: Y is an integral regular scheme of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] (the source's 'Y_red lisse'); f̄ : X̄ → Y is projective and smooth of pure relative dimension 1; D ⊂ X̄ is a divisor finite étale over Y; X = X̄ − D with f = f̄|X; and ℱ is a lisse sheaf on X, punctually pure of weight n and tamely ramified along D. Then Theorem 3.3.1 holds for every separated morphism of schemes of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] and every sheaf mixed of weights ≤ n. The same reduction holds for ι-mixed sheaves with real weights.
hypotheses: Separated finite-type morphisms over ℤ[1/ℓ]
Noetherian induction on Y and induction on the relative dimension of f

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Reduction step: Let f : X → Y be a separated morphism of schemes of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] and n ∈ ℤ. Say that a sheaf ℱ on X satisfies P_n(f) when R^i f_!ℱ is mixed of weights ≤ n + i for every i. (a) For an exact sequence 0 → ℱ′ → ℱ → ℱ″ → 0: P_n(f) for ℱ′ and ℱ″ implies P_n(f) for ℱ; P_n(f) for ℱ and ℱ″ implies P_n(f) for ℱ′; if the sequence splits, P_n(f) for ℱ implies P_n(f) for ℱ′. (b) If j : U → X is open with closed complement i : S → X, then P_n(f∘j) for j*ℱ and P_n(f∘i) for i*ℱ imply P_n(f) for ℱ. (f) If f is quasi-finite and ℱ is punctually pure of weight m, then f_!ℱ = R⁰f_!ℱ is punctually pure of weight m and R^i f_!ℱ = 0 for i ≠ 0; hence, by (a), every mixed ℱ of weights ≤ n satisfies P_n(f) when f is quasi-finite. The same statements hold with 'mixed of weights ≤ n + i' replaced by 'ι-mixed of ι-weights ≤ β + i' (β ∈ ℝ) and, for X over 𝔽_q, for Weil sheaves.

Reduction step: Use the just-defined P_n(f). (c) Let j : V → Y be open with closed complement i : T → Y, and f_V, f_T the base changes of f. Then ℱ satisfies P_n(f) iff ℱ|X_V satisfies P_n(f_V) and ℱ|X_T satisfies P_n(f_T). More generally, a sheaf 𝒢 on Y is mixed of weights ≤ m iff 𝒢|V and 𝒢|T are. (d) If f = g ∘ h with h : X → Z and g : Z → Y separated of finite type, and R^p g_! R^q h_!ℱ is mixed of weights ≤ n + p + q for all p, q, then ℱ satisfies P_n(f); in particular P_n(h) for ℱ together with P_{n+q}(g) for every R^q h_!ℱ implies P_n(f). (e) If g : Y′ → Y is a universal homeomorphism (integral, radicial, surjective), f′ : X′ → Y′ the base change and ℱ′ the pullback of ℱ, then ℱ satisfies P_n(f) iff ℱ′ satisfies P_n(f′); examples: Y′ = Y_red, and for Y normal integral, the normalisation of Y in a purely inseparable extension of its function field. The same statements hold for ι-mixed sheaves with real weights.

(c) Proper base change for Rf_! (SF.2, EDC.0) identifies (R^i f_!ℱ)|V = R^i f_{V!}(ℱ|X_V) and (R^i f_!ℱ)|T = R^i f_{T!}(ℱ|X_T). For a sheaf 𝒢, 0 → j_!j*𝒢 → 𝒢 → i_*i*𝒢 → 0 is exact and j_!, i_* preserve mixedness and weights (extension by zero and closed pushforward do not change the nonzero stalks), so 𝒢 is an extension of mixed sheaves of weights ≤ m.

(d) The Leray spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = R^p g_! R^q h_!ℱ ⇒ R^{p+q} f_!ℱ (EDC.0) has finitely many nonzero terms; E_∞^{pq} is a subquotient of E_2^{pq}, hence mixed of weights ≤ n + p + q, and R^k f_!ℱ has a finite filtration with quotients E_∞^{p,k−p}.
(e) Topological invariance of the étale site (SF.2) gives Rf′_!ℱ′ = g*Rf_!ℱ; g is a bijection on closed points with equal finite residue fields, so a sheaf 𝒢 on Y is mixed of weights ≤ m iff g*𝒢 is.

(a) Apply the long exact sequence of R^•f_!. For the second clause, R^i f_!ℱ′ is an extension of a subsheaf of R^i f_!ℱ by a quotient of R^{i−1}f_!ℱ″, which is mixed of weights ≤ n + i − 1 ≤ n + i; conclude by the stabilities of EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness. In the split case R^i f_!ℱ′ is a direct summand of R^i f_!ℱ.
(b) Apply (a) to 0 → j_!j*ℱ → ℱ → i_*i*ℱ → 0 with Rf_!j_! = R(fj)_! and Rf_!i_* = R(fi)_! (EDC.0).

(f) For f quasi-finite and separated, R^i f_! = 0 for i ≠ 0 and the stalk of f_!ℱ at a geometric point ȳ over y ∈ |Y| is ⊕_{x ↦ y} Ind(ℱ_x̄), the sum over the closed points x of the fibre of the modules induced from ⟨F_x⟩ = ⟨F_y^{d_x}⟩, d_x = [k(x) : k(y)] (proper base change, SF.2). The eigenvalues of F_y on an induced module are the d_x-th roots of the eigenvalues of F_x, and α^{d} is a Weil N(y)^{d}-number of weight m iff α is a Weil N(y)-number of weight m (EDC.7/weight-weil-number-base-extension); N(x) = N(y)^{d_x}.
The ι-variant uses the same steps with EDC.7/weight-iota-weight, which satisfies w_{q^r}(α^r) = w_q(α).

Dévissages (b), (c), (d) reduce to f of relative dimension ≤ 1: factor f locally on X through an affine space over Y, decompose by coordinate projections into morphisms of relative dimension ≤ 1, and use (d); (f) disposes of relative dimension 0. Dévissages (a), (b) reduce to ℱ lisse and punctually pure of weight n on X, by the defining filtration of a mixed sheaf and a stratification of X on whose strata ℱ is lisse.

By (c) and noetherian induction on Y it suffices to prove the conclusion over a dense open of each irreducible component of Y. Let η be a generic point of Y and apply EDC.7/weight-tame-cover-of-a-lisse-sheaf-on-a-curve to the generic fibre X_η and ℱ|X_η, after a finite purely inseparable extension of k(η).

Spread out C′, D̄, E, u and the direct-summand splitting to a dense open of the normalisation of Y_red in that purely inseparable extension, by finite-presentation limit arguments for polarised relative curves (tauceti ModularCurves 0E, AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2); shrink so that the open is regular (the regular locus of an excellent integral scheme is a dense open) and D̄ → Y is projective and smooth, E finite étale, u finite étale and u*ℱ tamely ramified along E (tameness spreads out from the generic points of E because the ramification is controlled by the pro-ℓ monodromy group Γ of the previous node).

By (e) the purely inseparable base change is harmless; by (b), (f), (a) the finitely many points removed in (α) do not matter and ℱ|C′ may be replaced by its summand-carrier u_*u*ℱ, i.e. by u*ℱ on D, since Rf_!u_* = R(fu)_!.

Non-example: the reduction does not assume f̄ proper from the start; a nonproper X is compactified only after the reduction to a relative curve.
Acceptance: for f = id the class P_n contains exactly the sheaves mixed of weights ≤ n.

Acceptance: for the finite étale double cover Spec 𝔽_{q²} → Spec 𝔽_q and ℱ = ℚ̄_ℓ, f_*ℚ̄_ℓ has F-eigenvalues ±1 (weight 0), not 1 with multiplicity 2: (f) computes induced modules, not sums of copies.

nodes.title: Generic smoothness and tame covers of a lisse sheaf on a curve (Weil II (α), (β))
nodes.statement: Let K be a field in which ℓ is invertible, C a separated K-scheme of finite type of dimension 1, and ℱ a lisse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaf on C. After replacing K by a finite purely inseparable extension (none is needed if K is perfect): (α) there is a finite set Σ of closed points of C_red such that C′ = C_red − Σ is smooth over K; (β) there are a smooth projective curve D̄ over K, a reduced divisor E ⊂ D̄ étale over K, and a finite étale surjective morphism u : D = D̄ − E → C′ such that u*ℱ is tamely ramified along E, and ℱ|C′ is a direct summand of u_*u*ℱ = Ru_*u*ℱ.
hypotheses: ℓ invertible in K; ℱ lisse on C; C of dimension 1
The direct-summand statement uses ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients: the trace u_*u* → id composed with the adjunction is multiplication by the degree on each component, invertible in ℚ̄_ℓ

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Work first over the perfect closure K^perf (K itself if perfect). Remove all zero-dimensional components and the finitely many nonsmooth points of the reduced one-dimensional components. The remaining C′ is a smooth curve.

The lisse sheaf has a continuous representation with a stable O_A-lattice for a finite extension A/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.0). The congruence subgroup ker(GL_r(O_A) → GL_r(O_A/ℓ²)) is open and pro-ℓ. Its inverse image defines a finite étale surjective cover u : D → C′, separately on each component.

Over K^perf use the smooth projective models of the components of D (tauceti AlgebraicCurves layer 12). Their finite reduced boundaries E are étale over this perfect field. At each boundary trait wild inertia is pro-p (or trivial in characteristic zero); its continuous image in the pro-ℓ congruence subgroup is trivial since p ≠ ℓ. Thus u*ℱ is tame (LPV.1, the geometric-trait inertia request below).

Descend the finite-presentation data C′, u, D̄ and E to some finite purely inseparable K′/K. Enlarge K′ if needed so that smoothness, properness, the open immersion D ⊂ D̄, the finite étale surjective cover and the étale boundary hold there. Topological invariance of the étale site under purely inseparable base change identifies the sheaves and inertia actions and preserves tameness (SF.2). This does not assert that K′ is perfect.
For u finite étale, u_* = u_! = Ru_*; the composite of adjunction and trace is multiplication by the componentwise degree, invertible in ℚ̄_ℓ. Divide the trace by that degree to split ℱ|C′ → u_*u*ℱ.
acceptance: Acceptance: for K = 𝔽_q, C = 𝔾_m and ℱ the Kummer sheaf of a character of order prime to p, u can be taken to be the identity: ℱ is already tame at 0 and ∞.
Acceptance: for the Artin–Schreier sheaf L_ψ on 𝔸¹_{𝔽_p}, which is wildly ramified at ∞, u is a nontrivial cover (its pullback to the Artin–Schreier cover y^p − y = x becomes trivial, hence tame).

Non-example: over K = 𝔽_p(t), the regular curve C = Spec K[x,y]/(y^p−t) is nowhere smooth over K, since its constant field is purely inseparable over K. After K′=K(t^{1/p}) and reduction, it becomes 𝔸¹_{K′}. Thus the purely inseparable extension in (α) cannot be omitted; a curve that is merely nonsmooth at finitely many points would not test this necessity.

nodes.title: Rf_! preserves complexes of weights ≤ w
nodes.statement: Let f : X₀ → Y₀ be a morphism of schemes of finite type over 𝔽_q. If K ∈ D^b_c(X₀) is mixed of weights ≤ w, then Rf_!K is mixed of weights ≤ w. The ι-variant holds with w ∈ ℝ.
hypotheses: f separated of finite type (Rf_! as in EDC.0)

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Use the spectral sequence E₂^{pq} = R^pf_!ℋ^qK ⇒ ℋ^{p+q}Rf_!K (printed E₁, PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E70).

By EDC.7/weight-fundamental-direct-image-theorem-3-3-1, E₂^{pq} is mixed of punctual weights ≤ p + (q + w); the abutment ℋ^{p+q}Rf_!K has a finite filtration with subquotients of the E₂^{pq}, hence is mixed of punctual weights ≤ (p + q) + w.
The ι-variant uses EDC.7/weight-iota-mixed-direct-image-3-3-10.

nodes.title: R^i f_* of a mixed sheaf is mixed
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes of finite type over 𝔽_p (Weil sheaves), or of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] in the context of Weil II (6.1.1) b) (after inverting finitely many primes), and ℱ a mixed sheaf on X. Then every R^i f_*ℱ is mixed.
hypotheses: Contexts (6.1.1) a) and b) only
No weight bound is asserted for Rf_*: only mixedness

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: By the generic base change theorem (SGA 4½ [Th. finitude] 1.9, supplied by EDC.0), applied with S = Y, the formation of R^i f_*ℱ commutes with base change over a dense open of Y; by noetherian induction on Y and dévissage (c) of EDC.7/weight-spreading-out-to-a-tame-relative-curve (localisation on the base preserves mixedness of a sheaf) it suffices to know mixedness over a dense open of each stratum.
Over a dense open this is EDC.7/weight-generic-mixedness-of-direct-images-6-1-3 applied to S = Y (or to the stratum), with f viewed as a morphism of S-schemes.

(6.1.10) Locally on Y and, through the Leray spectral sequence of an affine cover, on X: factor f = g∘j with j an open immersion and g proper; Rg_* = Rg_! preserves mixedness by EDC.7/weight-fundamental-direct-image-theorem-3-3-1 and Rj_* by the case (∗)_n of the lemma.
acceptance: Acceptance: j : 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹ over 𝔽_q, ℱ = ℚ̄_ℓ: j_*ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ (weight 0) and R¹j_*ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)_0 (weight 2): mixed, with weights above those of ℱ + i allowed.
Non-example: Rf_* does not preserve the upper weight bound: R¹j_*ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 2 > 0 + 1.

nodes.title: Weight estimates for the six operations
nodes.statement: Let f : X₀ → Y₀ be a morphism of schemes of finite type over 𝔽_q, and a, b, w ∈ ℤ. (i) f* and Rf_! carry complexes of weights ≤ w to complexes of weights ≤ w. (ii) Rf_* and Rf^! carry complexes of weights ≥ w to complexes of weights ≥ w. (iii) D exchanges 'weights ≤ w' and 'weights ≥ −w'. (iv) If K has weights ≤ a and L has weights ≤ b, then K ⊗ L has weights ≤ a + b. (v) If K has weights ≤ a and L has weights ≥ b, then RHom(K, L) has weights ≥ b − a. The ι-variants hold with real weights. No other preservation is asserted: Rf_* and Rf^! need not preserve upper bounds, f* and Rf_! need not preserve lower bounds, and a pure complex need not split into its cohomology sheaves.
hypotheses: Finite type over 𝔽_q; mixed complexes
Each functor preserves one bound only

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: (i) f*: for y ∈ |X₀| over x = f(y), F_y acts on (f*ℋ^iK)_ȳ = ℋ^i(K)_x̄ as F_x^{[k(y):k(x)]} and N(y) = N(x)^{[k(y):k(x)]}, so weights are unchanged (EDC.7/weight-weil-number-base-extension); mixedness passes by (1.2.5). Rf_!: EDC.7/weight-compact-support-direct-image-upper-weights-6-2-3.
(iii) is the definition of weights ≥ (EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes) together with biduality (EDC.1). (ii) Rf_* = D Rf_! D and Rf^! = D f* D (EDC.1 exchange isomorphisms), then (i) and (iii).

(iv) The spectral sequence of the canonical filtrations gives ℋ^n(K ⊗ L) a finite filtration with subquotients of ⊕_{i+j=n} ℋ^iK ⊗ ℋ^jL (no Tor terms over a field, EDC.0); tensor products of mixed sheaves are mixed with weights adding (1.2.5), so ℋ^n has weights ≤ (a + i) + (b + j) = a + b + n.
(v) RHom(K, L) = D(K ⊗ DL) by D(K ⊗ M) = RHom(K, DM) with M = DL and biduality; K ⊗ DL has weights ≤ a − b by (iii), (iv), so its dual has weights ≥ b − a.
acceptance: Non-example: for j : 𝔾_m → ℙ¹ and ℚ̄_ℓ (pure of weight 0 on 𝔾_m), Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ is not of weights ≤ 0 (R¹j_* has weight 2 > 0 + 1), and j_!ℚ̄_ℓ is not of weights ≥ 0 (its dual Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ(1)[2] has ℋ^{−1} of weight 0 > −0 − 1).
Acceptance: for X₀ smooth proper and K pure of weight w, (i) and (ii) together give purity of Rf_*K = Rf_!K (EDC.7/weight-proper-direct-image-preserves-purity-6-2-6).
Acceptance: for L lisse pure of weight b on smooth X₀ and K = ℚ̄_ℓ (pure of weight 0), RHom(ℚ̄_ℓ, L) = L has weights ≥ b.

nodes.title: Generic mixedness of R^i f_* over a base of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ]
nodes.statement: Let S be a scheme of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ], f : X → Y a morphism of S-schemes of finite type, and ℱ a mixed sheaf on X. Then there is a dense open U ⊂ S over which all the sheaves R^i f_*ℱ are mixed.
hypotheses: S of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ]; f of finite type; ℱ mixed
Only a dense open of S: no claim over all of S

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: (6.1.4) If X is smooth over Y = S, ℱ lisse and all R^i f_!ℱ^∨ lisse, then R^i f_*ℱ is obtained from R^{2N−i} f_!(ℱ^∨)(N) by relative Poincaré duality (EDC.2, componentwise of relative dimension N), and the latter is mixed by EDC.7/weight-fundamental-direct-image-theorem-3-3-1.
(6.1.5) If X is smooth over Y = S and ℱ lisse, shrink S so that the R^i f_!ℱ^∨ are lisse (generic constructibility and local constancy, EDC.0) and apply (6.1.4).

(6.1.6)–(6.1.8) Induct on n = dim X_η for open immersions with dense image and S integral. The base n=0 becomes X=Y after shrinking S. In 6.1.7 coordinate projections and induction give mixedness on an open Y′⊂Y whose complement Y₁ is finite over S. For 6.1.8 assume X smooth over S and ℱ lisse; compactify Y over S, with structure b:Y→S, and let j:Y′→Y and i:Y₁→Y. Applying Rb_* to j_!j*Rf_*ℱ → Rf_*ℱ → i_*i*Rf_*ℱ gives a triangle whose first term is mixed by 3.3.1 and the already mixed restriction on Y′, and whose second is R(bf)_*ℱ, mixed by 6.1.5. Thus R(bi)_*i*Rf_*ℱ is mixed. Since bi is finite, its pushforward is exact and reflects mixedness: any sheaf injects into its pullback-pushforward along this finite map, and mixedness is stable under pullback and subobjects. Hence i*Rf_*ℱ is mixed and gluing with Y′ finishes 6.1.8. The finite morphism interface is EDC.7/weight-spreading-out-to-a-tame-relative-curve.

(6.1.9) After a finite radicial surjective base change choose j : V → X dense, with V smooth over S and j*ℱ lisse. Apply 6.1.8 to j and to f∘j. Let A be the cone of ℱ → Rj_*j*ℱ, not the cone of j_!j*ℱ → ℱ. Its cohomology is mixed because ℱ and Rj_*j*ℱ are mixed, and is supported on X−V of smaller generic dimension. Induction makes Rf_*A mixed; the triangle Rf_*ℱ → R(fj)_*j*ℱ → Rf_*A then proves the desired mixedness. Universal-homeomorphism invariance descends the result (SF.2).

The derived-category arguments are justified at finite level: write ℱ through a projective system of locally free ℤ/ℓ^n-sheaves as in Weil II (1.1.1) and apply the same triangles levelwise (EDC.0's adic formalism).

General f: the problem is local on Y and, by the Leray spectral sequence of an affine cover of X, on X; factor an affine f as an open immersion followed by a proper morphism (Nagata, EDC.0) and combine (∗)_n with 3.3.1.
acceptance: Acceptance: S = Spec ℤ[1/ℓ], f : 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹ the inclusion over S, ℱ = ℚ̄_ℓ: R¹f_*ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) at 0, mixed of weight 2 over every closed point of S.
Non-example: the conclusion is generic on S; it does not assert that a constructible sheaf on X_ℚ comes from a mixed sheaf on some X[1/n] (Weil II (6.1.1) b) records that this is unknown).

nodes.title: Geometric monodromy and geometrically semisimple lisse sheaves
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be a connected normal scheme of finite type over 𝔽_q, X = X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, x̄ a geometric point of X. The arithmetic and geometric fundamental groups π₁(X₀, x̄) ⊃ π₁(X, x̄) fit into 1 → π₁(X, x̄) → π₁(X₀, x̄) → Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) → 1 (for X₀ geometrically connected; IG.1), and the Weil group W(X₀, x̄) is the preimage of the subgroup generated by the geometric Frobenius F. A lisse ℚ̄_ℓ-(Weil) sheaf ℱ₀ is a continuous representation ρ of W(X₀, x̄) on V = ℱ_x̄ (EDC.0). Its geometric monodromy group is ρ(π₁(X, x̄)) ⊂ GL(V) (Weil II 1.1.15). ℱ₀ is geometrically semisimple when the pullback ℱ on X is semisimple, i.e. ρ|π₁(X, x̄) is a semisimple representation (V is a direct sum of irreducible π₁(X, x̄)-subrepresentations); it is arithmetically semisimple when ρ is semisimple. For X₀ not geometrically connected, apply the definitions on each connected component of X.
hypotheses: X₀ normal, so that π₁ of a dense open surjects onto π₁(X₀) and lisse sheaves are representations
Semisimplicity of the restriction to the geometric fundamental group, not of the arithmetic representation

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Ordinary lisse sheaves on normal connected X₀ correspond to continuous finite-dimensional π₁(X₀)-representations; compactness gives a stable lattice over a finite coefficient extension. For lisse Weil sheaves use W(X₀); only its profinite geometric subgroup is required to preserve such a lattice, while the chosen Frobenius may act by any invertible ℓ-adic scalar (Weil II 1.1.14, EDC.0, IG.0).

The socle (sum of irreducible subrepresentations) of ρ|π₁(X, x̄) is stable under W(X₀, x̄) because π₁(X, x̄) is normal in it; so geometric semisimplicity is a property of ℱ₀, and the maximal geometrically semisimple lisse subsheaf descends to X₀.

For the arithmetic-to-geometric semisimplicity API, finite-dimensionality gives a finite sum of irreducible W-representations. Apply the pinned Tau Ceti Clifford theorem isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype to each normal-subgroup restriction and take their finite direct sum; this imports the existing theorem rather than planning Clifford theory again.
acceptance: Over Spec 𝔽_q every lisse sheaf is geometrically semisimple (π₁ of Spec 𝔽̄_q is trivial).
Arithmetic semisimplicity implies geometric semisimplicity (Clifford's argument for the normal subgroup π₁(X, x̄)).

complete reducibility of the monodromy representation on H^{n−1}(Y) makes the cup-product form nondegenerate on invariants
geometric monodromy of a pure lisse sheaf is semisimple, so its Zariski closure has reductive identity component

geometric semisimplicity of perverse direct images

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsGeometricallySemisimple.dual
api.statement: The dual of a geometrically semisimple lisse sheaf is geometrically semisimple.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.maximalGeometricallySemisimpleSubsheaf
api.statement: The largest geometrically semisimple lisse subsheaf (sum of the irreducible lisse subsheaves of ℱ), stable under Frobenius and hence defined over X₀.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.isGeometricallySemisimple_iff_reductive
api.statement: With algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficients and finite-dimensional stalk: ℱ₀ is geometrically semisimple iff the identity component of the Zariski closure of its geometric monodromy group is reductive (tauceti ReductiveGroups layer 6). The closure acts faithfully; invariant subspaces are unchanged by Zariski closure.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.mem_geometricMonodromyGroup
api.statement: A linear automorphism a belongs to geometricMonodromyGroup ρ G iff a = ρ g for some g ∈ G. When stored as an endomorphism submonoid, every element is invertible since G is a group.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.geometricMonodromyGroup_conjugate
api.statement: An isomorphism of stalk representations conjugates the geometric monodromy image; changing the geometric base point gives this conjugacy, so geometric semisimplicity is independent of the base point.

nodes.title: Mixed complexes and complexes of weights ≤ w
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be a scheme of finite type over 𝔽_q (Weil II (6.1.1) a): sheaves are ℚ̄_ℓ-Weil sheaves) and D^b_c(X₀) the bounded derived category of constructible ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaves on X₀ of EDC.0, with cohomology sheaves ℋ^i. A complex K ∈ D^b_c(X₀) is mixed when every ℋ^iK is mixed (EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness); D^b_m(X₀) ⊂ D^b_c(X₀) is the full subcategory of mixed complexes. For w ∈ ℤ, K is mixed of weights ≤ w when, for every i, ℋ^iK is mixed of punctual weights ≤ w + i (Weil II 6.2.2); D^b_{≤w}(X₀) denotes the full subcategory of such K. For a fixed field isomorphism ι : ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ and w ∈ ℝ, 'ι-mixed of ι-weights ≤ w' is defined in the same way from EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness. For X of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] (context (6.1.1) b), and Weil II 6.2.7) the same definitions apply to constructible ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaves.
hypotheses: X₀ of finite type over 𝔽_q; ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients, ℓ ∤ q
The shift convention: ℋ^iK is allowed weights up to w + i, not w

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: D^b_m(X₀) is a strictly full triangulated subcategory: it is closed under isomorphism and shifts, and if K′ → K → K″ → K′[1] is distinguished with two of the three terms mixed, the long exact sequence of cohomology sheaves exhibits each ℋ^i of the third as an extension of a subsheaf by a quotient of mixed sheaves (stabilities, EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness).
The same argument shows that if K′ and K″ have weights ≤ w then so has K; direct summands of objects of weights ≤ w have weights ≤ w.
For a mixed sheaf the punctual weights are ≤ m iff every eigenvalue of every F_x on the stalks has weight ≤ m: a nonzero constructible sheaf has a nonzero stalk at a closed point.
acceptance: On Spec 𝔽_q, K has weights ≤ w iff for every i the Frobenius module H^i(K) has all weights ≤ w + i (EDC.7/weight-endomorphism-weights).

uses.how: Rf_! preserves complexes of weights ≤ n; the definition is designed so that 3.3.1 gives this through the spectral sequence R^pf_!ℋ^qK ⇒ ℋ^{p+q}Rf_!K
a pure complex is one of weights ≤ n whose dual has weights ≤ −n
purity of IC_X(L) of weight w + d and of perverse direct images is stated with this weight convention
imports the complex weight formalism and the normalisation F[a](b) of weight r + a − 2b
bounded-weight terms in long exact sequences of complexes

tests.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsLE_zero
tests.statement: The zero complex is mixed and has weights ≤ w for every w.

tests.name: TauCeti.Weights.not_isMixedComplex_transcendental
tests.statement: On Spec 𝔽_q, the rank-one Weil sheaf on which F acts by a transcendental b ∈ ℚ̄_ℓ^× is not mixed (its eigenvalue is not a Weil number), although it is ι-mixed for every ι.

tests.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsLE_point_iff
tests.statement: On Spec 𝔽_q, K has weights ≤ w iff every eigenvalue of F on every H^i(K) is a Weil q-number of weight ≤ w + i, i.e. iff each Frobenius module H^i(K) has the EDC.7 Frobenius-module weight targets weights ≤ w + i.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsMixedComplex
api.statement: IsMixedComplex K : Prop := ∀ i, IsMixed (ℋ^i K), for K in the bounded constructible derived category of EDC.0.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.HasWeightsLE
api.statement: HasWeightsLE (w : ℤ) K : Prop := ∀ i, IsMixed (ℋ^i K) ∧ ∀ weight m of ℋ^i K, m ≤ w + i.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.HasIotaWeightsLE
api.statement: The ι-variant with w : ℝ and EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.isMixedComplex_triangle
api.statement: D^b_m is a triangulated subcategory: two out of three terms of a distinguished triangle mixed ⇒ the third is; closed under shifts and direct summands.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.HasWeightsLE.of_triangle
api.statement: For a distinguished triangle K′ → K → K″ →: K′, K″ of weights ≤ w ⇒ K of weights ≤ w.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsLE_shift
api.statement: HasWeightsLE (w + 1) (K[1]) ↔ HasWeightsLE w K: ℋ^i(K[1]) = ℋ^{i+1}K.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsLE_twist
api.statement: K(r) has weights ≤ w − 2r iff K has weights ≤ w; in particular K(N)[2N] has weights ≤ w iff K has (Weil II 6.2.5 a).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.HasWeightsLE.mono
api.statement: w ≤ w′ → HasWeightsLE w K → HasWeightsLE w′ K.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsLE_sheaf_iff
api.statement: A sheaf ℱ placed in degree 0 has weights ≤ w iff ℱ is mixed of punctual weights ≤ w.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsLE_iff_eigenvalues
api.statement: For mixed K: K has weights ≤ w iff for all i and x ∈ |X₀| every eigenvalue of F_x on ℋ^i(K)_x̄ has weight ≤ w + i relative to N(x).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsLE_baseExtension
api.statement: Weights are unchanged by the base extension 𝔽_q → 𝔽_{q^r} (EDC.7/weight-finite-field-base-extension-of-weights).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.HasWeightsLE.isIotaWeightsLE
api.statement: A complex of weights ≤ w has ι-weights ≤ w for every ι.

nodes.title: Sheaves and complexes potentially having a property P
nodes.statement: Let P be a property of sheaves (or of complexes) on schemes of finite type over finite fields, for example 'mixed', 'punctually ι-pure of weight β', or 'pure of weight w' in the sense of EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes. Let k be an algebraically closed field with ℓ invertible in k and X a scheme of finite type over k. A sheaf ℱ (resp. a complex K ∈ D^b_c(X)) has potentially the property P when there is a model: an integral scheme S of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ], a morphism x̄ : Spec k → S, a scheme X_S of finite type over S, a sheaf ℱ_S (resp. complex K_S) on X_S, and an isomorphism of (X_S, ℱ_S) ×_S Spec k (base change along x̄) with (X, ℱ), such that for every closed point s ∈ |S| the restriction of ℱ_S (resp. K_S) to the fibre X_s, a scheme of finite type over the finite field k(s), has the property P. A model is part of the data of a proof that ℱ is potentially P; it is not an existence label.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed, ℓ invertible
S of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ]; the condition is at all closed points of S
For complexes and P = pure, duality on the fibres is relative to k(s)
P is invariant under isomorphism. Base-field-extension and finite-sum stability of P are separate hypotheses of the corresponding API lemmas.

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Definition. Shrinking S to a dense open neighbourhood of the image of x̄ preserves the property (closed points of an open of S are closed in S), so models can always be refined.

The arithmetic sheaf or complex model is an input witnessing potential P; this definition does not assert that every constructible ℓ-adic sheaf has a finite-type arithmetic model. L2 supplies noetherian approximation for schemes, morphisms and finite-presentation or finite-coefficient data, and refinements of models already given. This distinction is explicit in Weil II 6.1.1 b).
acceptance: Over k = 𝔽̄_q, a sheaf defined over a finite subfield 𝔽_{q^r} with property P is potentially P (take S = Spec 𝔽_{q^r}).

uses.how: potentially punctually ι-pure lisse sheaves on normal X over k algebraically closed are semisimple
hard Lefschetz for potentially pure complexes
the potentially pure complexes of 6.2.8–6.2.12, with their arithmetic model over a finite-type ℤ[1/ℓ]-base
ℚ̄_ℓ on a smooth projective variety over any algebraically closed field is potentially pure, through an arithmetic model

tests.name: TauCeti.Weights.potentiallyPure_const_smooth
tests.statement: For X smooth over k algebraically closed, ℚ̄_ℓ[0] is potentially pure of weight 0: spread X out to X_S smooth over S, and ℚ̄_ℓ on each smooth fibre is pure (EDC.7/weight-twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5).

tests.name: TauCeti.Weights.potentially_of_finite_field
tests.statement: Over k = 𝔽̄_q, a sheaf ℱ₀ on X₀/𝔽_q with property P is potentially P with model S = Spec 𝔽_q.

tests.name: TauCeti.Weights.not_potentiallyPure_kummer
tests.statement: A unipotent Kummer local system on 𝔾_m over ℂ admits a model with nontrivial geometric extension and mixed Tate graded pieces; this witness establishes potentially mixed. Its witness is not punctually pure, since its nonzero graded weights differ. This test rejects treating every supplied mixed model as a supplied pure model; it makes no assertion about all other models.

tests.name: TauCeti.Weights.potentially_zero
tests.statement: The zero sheaf is potentially P for every P satisfied by zero sheaves, with any model.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.ArithmeticModel
api.statement: The data (S, x̄, X_S, ℱ_S or K_S, iso) of a model of (X, ℱ) over an integral S of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ].

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.PotentiallyHas
api.statement: PotentiallyHas P ℱ : Prop := ∃ M : ArithmeticModel X ℱ, ∀ s ∈ |M.S|, P (M.ℱ_S|X_s).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.PotentiallyHas.mono
api.statement: (∀ ℱ, P ℱ → Q ℱ) → PotentiallyHas P ℱ → PotentiallyHas Q ℱ.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.ArithmeticModel.restrict
api.statement: Restrict a model to a dense open of S containing the image of x̄; the fibrewise property is inherited.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.PotentiallyHas.pullback
api.statement: If g : Y → X spreads out over a model, then g*ℱ is potentially P whenever ℱ is and P is stable under pullback.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.PotentiallyHas.directSum
api.statement: If the supplied arithmetic witnesses admit a common refinement and P is stable under finite direct sums and finite extensions of finite ground fields, their finite direct sum is potentially P. Pull the witnesses to this common model, use finite-field-extension stability on its closed fibres, and take the direct sum there. A common refinement of arbitrary ℓ-adic sheaf models is not silently asserted.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.potentially_baseChange_algClosed
api.statement: For an extension k ⊂ k′ of algebraically closed fields, PotentiallyHas P ℱ implies PotentiallyHas P ℱ_{k′}, using the same model and composing x̄ with Spec k′ → Spec k. The converse requires a witnessing model over k′ whose base-point map and fibre identification descend to k; no unconditional converse for arbitrary P is asserted.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.PotentiallyHas.of_iso
api.statement: For P invariant under isomorphism, an isomorphism of (X,ℱ) with (X′,ℱ′) transports an ArithmeticModel and gives PotentiallyHas P ℱ ↔ PotentiallyHas P ℱ′.

nodes.title: Proper direct images of pure complexes are pure
nodes.statement: Let f : X₀ → Y₀ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over 𝔽_q and K ∈ D^b_c(X₀) pure of weight w. Then Rf_*K is pure of weight w. In particular, for X₀ proper over 𝔽_q and K pure of weight w, H^i(X, K) is pure of weight w + i for every i. The ι-variant holds.
hypotheses: f proper

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Rf_* = Rf_! for f proper; Rf_!K has weights ≤ w by EDC.7/weight-compact-support-direct-image-upper-weights-6-2-3.
D Rf_*K = Rf_! DK (EDC.1, f proper), and DK has weights ≤ −w, so DRf_*K has weights ≤ −w.
For Y₀ = Spec 𝔽_q, a complex is pure of weight w iff each H^i is pure of weight w + i (EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes test isPureComplex_point_iff).
acceptance: Acceptance: X₀ smooth proper, K = ℚ̄_ℓ: H^i pure of weight i, giving the smooth proper cohomology statement.

Acceptance: X₀ = ℙ¹, K = j_*ℱ for a pure lisse ℱ on an open curve. Weil II 6.2.5(c), p.248, makes the complex j_*ℱ pure; proper direct-image purity then gives H¹(ℙ¹, j_*ℱ) pure, agreeing with EDC.7/weight-sharp-curve-purity.
Non-example: for f non-proper, e.g. 𝔾_m → Spec 𝔽_q and K = ℚ̄_ℓ, Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ is not pure (H¹ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weight 2 ≠ 1).

sources.match: Apply compact-support upper weights to K and DK and use proper duality exchange for both bounds.

nodes.title: Complexes of weights ≥ w and pure complexes
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be of finite type over 𝔽_q, a : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q, K_{X₀} = Ra^!ℚ̄_ℓ the dualizing complex and D = RHom(−, K_{X₀}) the duality functor of EDC.1, which is involutive on D^b_c(X₀), exchanges f* with Rf^! and Rf_* with Rf_!, and satisfies D(K ⊗ L) = RHom(K, DL). A complex K is mixed of weights ≥ w when DK is mixed of weights ≤ −w (EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes). K is pure of weight w when it is mixed of weights ≤ w and of weights ≥ w (Weil II 6.2.4). A sheaf ℱ is pure of weight w when the complex ℱ[0] is. The ι-variants (w ∈ ℝ) are defined in the same way. On X₀ smooth of pure dimension d, K_{X₀} = ℚ̄_ℓ(d)[2d] (EDC.2), so K has weights ≥ w iff RHom(K, ℚ̄_ℓ) has weights ≤ −w.
hypotheses: D is Verdier duality relative to Spec 𝔽_q (EDC.1), not absolute Galois duality
Purity of a complex is a condition on K and on DK; on a singular X₀ it is not a stalkwise condition

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Well-definedness only uses the existence of D (EDC.1); DK is mixed when K is (EDC.7/weight-six-operations-preserve-mixedness-6-1-11), so 'weights ≥ w' is a condition on mixed complexes.

Closure properties: since D is a triangulated anti-equivalence, the class of complexes of weights ≥ w is closed under extensions, shifts K ≥ w ⇔ K[1] ≥ w + 1 and twists K ≥ w ⇔ K(r) ≥ w − 2r, as for ≤ w.
By biduality D² ≅ id (EDC.1), K is pure of weight w iff DK is pure of weight −w.
acceptance: On Spec 𝔽_q, D is the linear dual (K_X = ℚ̄_ℓ), and K is pure of weight w iff each H^i(K) is pure of weight w + i.

uses.how: proper direct image preserves purity: apply 6.2.3 to K and DK
hard Lefschetz for potentially pure complexes
the local and global invariant cycle theorems 6.2.9 and 6.2.12 for pure complexes
IC_X(L) is pure of weight w + d; purity of perverse direct images
on smooth X with lisse cohomology, purity of weight w iff H^i pointwise pure of weight w + i

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.HasWeightsGE
api.statement: HasWeightsGE (w : ℤ) K : Prop := HasWeightsLE (−w) (D K).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsPureComplex

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.hasWeightsGE_dual

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsPureComplex.dual
api.statement: IsPureComplex w K ↔ IsPureComplex (−w) (D K).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.HasWeightsGE.of_triangle

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsPureComplex.of_triangle

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.isPureComplex_iff_lisse

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsPureComplex.directSum
api.statement: A finite direct sum of pure complexes of weight w is pure of weight w; a sum containing two nonzero pure summands of distinct weights is mixed but cannot be pure of one weight. The zero complex is pure of every weight.

nodes.title: Stability of mixed complexes under the six operations and duality
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes of finite type over 𝔽_p (Weil sheaves), or in context (6.1.1) b). Then Rf_*, Rf_!, f* and Rf^! carry D^b_m to D^b_m; so do ⊗, the local RHom (and the local ℰxt^i), and the duality functor D. In particular the dualizing complex K_X = Ra^!ℚ̄_ℓ is mixed, and D^b_m(X) is stable under all the operations of EDC.0–EDC.1.
hypotheses: Contexts (6.1.1) a) and b)
Mixedness only: the weight estimates are EDC.7/weight-directional-weight-estimates

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: Rf_*: EDC.7/weight-direct-image-preserves-mixedness-6-1-2 and the spectral sequence R^pf_*ℋ^qK ⇒ ℋ^{p+q}Rf_*K. Rf_!: 3.3.1 and the same spectral sequence. f* and ⊗: stalks and the stabilities (1.2.5) (EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness); the Tor terms vanish over a field.

Rf^! first: locally factor f as a closed immersion i followed by a smooth morphism g of relative dimension N. Rg^! = g*(N)[2N] (EDC.2). For the complementary open j, the triangle i_*i^!L → L → Rj_*j*L (EDC.1) gives i^!L = i*(cone(L → Rj_*j*L))[−1], mixed by the already proved operations and stability under triangles (EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes).

RHom: stratify the first argument into extensions of j_!ℱ, where j : U → X is locally closed and ℱ is lisse. The correct adjunction is RHom(j_!ℱ,L) = Rj_*RHom(ℱ,j^!L) = Rj_*(ℱ^∨ ⊗ j^!L). Use the preceding Rf^! case, tensor, and Rf_*. For an open j, j^!=j*; this equality does not hold for an arbitrary locally closed immersion. Local ℰxt^i are the cohomology sheaves.
The dualizing complex K_X = Ra^!ℚ̄_ℓ is mixed by Rf^!, and D=RHom(−,K_X) preserves mixedness by the RHom case. This order avoids assuming RHom or duality stability while proving Rf^!.
acceptance: Acceptance: on a smooth X₀ of pure dimension d, K_{X₀} = ℚ̄_ℓ(d)[2d] is mixed, indeed pure of weight 0: ℋ^{−2d} = ℚ̄_ℓ(d) has weight −2d = 0 + (−2d).
Acceptance: for a closed point i : x → 𝔸¹ over 𝔽_q, i^!ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[−2] is mixed.

sources.match: Mixedness is stable under the six operations, duality and local Ext.

nodes.title: Purity on a smooth scheme is pointwise purity of lisse cohomology sheaves
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be of finite type over 𝔽_q. (a) For every N ∈ ℤ, K is mixed of weights ≤ w iff K(N)[2N] is; hence in the definition of purity the dualizing complex may be replaced by any complex locally isomorphic to K_{X₀}(N)[2N]. (b) If X₀ is smooth, K has weights ≥ w iff RHom(K, ℚ̄_ℓ) has weights ≤ −w. If moreover every ℋ^iK is lisse, K is pure of weight w iff every ℋ^iK is punctually pure of weight w + i. (c) Consequently, for X₀ smooth and ℱ₀ lisse and punctually pure of weight w, the complex ℱ₀[m](r) is pure of weight w + m − 2r. The ι-variants hold.
hypotheses: (b), (c): X₀ smooth; lisse cohomology sheaves
A stalkwise pure sheaf on a singular X₀ need not be pure (EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes, test not_isPureComplex_nodal)

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: (a) ℋ^i(K(N)[2N]) = ℋ^{i+2N}(K)(N), whose weights are those of ℋ^{i+2N}K minus 2N; so the bound w + (i + 2N) becomes w + i.

(b) On smooth X₀ of pure dimension d, K_{X₀} = ℚ̄_ℓ(d)[2d] (EDC.2), so DK = RHom(K, ℚ̄_ℓ)(d)[2d] and (a) applies. If the ℋ^iK are lisse, the local ℰxt^p(ℋ^iK, ℚ̄_ℓ) vanish for p > 0, so ℋ^{−i}RHom(K, ℚ̄_ℓ) = (ℋ^iK)^∨, mixed with the negatives of the weights of ℋ^iK (EDC.7/weight-spectra-of-tensor-products-and-duals). Thus K ≥ w iff every ℋ^iK has weights ≥ w + i, and together with K ≤ w iff every ℋ^iK has all weights equal to w + i, i.e. is punctually pure of weight w + i (a mixed sheaf all of whose weights equal m is an iterated extension of punctually pure sheaves of weight m, hence punctually pure).
(c) ℋ^{−m}(ℱ₀[m](r)) = ℱ₀(r), punctually pure of weight w − 2r = (w + m − 2r) + (−m); apply (b).

nodes.title: Positive even-tensor Euler products and comparison of poles
nodes.statement: Let F_x be finite-dimensional invertible Frobenius operators with det(1−tF_x)∈ℚ[t], or, for a fixed ι, with all power traces ι-real. For k≥1, Tr((F_x^n) on V_x^{⊗2k})=Tr(F_x^n on V_x)^{2k}≥0 after the specified embedding. Thus det(1−tF_x on V_x^{⊗2k})⁻¹ has nonnegative real coefficients, as does its substitution t↦t^{deg x}. More generally let f_i=1+Σ_(n≥1)a_(i,n)t^n have a_(i,n)≥0, with only finitely many f_i nontrivial modulo each t^N. The formal product f has coefficientwise f_i≤f and radius of absolute convergence R(f_i)≥R(f). If f and f_i extend meromorphically to ℂ and are holomorphic at 0, their nearest pole moduli satisfy the same inequality (the infimum of an empty pole set is ∞).
hypotheses: Even tensor exponent is positive. Local finiteness of the formal product and nonnegativity are indispensable; neither a symplectic pairing nor purity is needed for this comparison. Rational characteristic polynomials are a sufficient condition for real power traces, rather than an unnamed hypothesis of another theorem.
proofSteps: The logarithmic determinant identity gives log(det(1−tF)^−1)=Σ_(n≥1)Tr(F^n)t^n/n. Tensor trace multiplicativity makes the traces of positive even powers nonnegative. Exponentiating a zero-constant nonnegative series and substituting a positive integral degree preserve coefficientwise nonnegativity.

In a locally finite formal product, the coefficient a_(i,n) occurs with all other factors contributing their constant term 1; all other summands are nonnegative. Comparison of the absolute series proves the radius bound.

A Taylor series of a function meromorphic on ℂ has radius the distance to its nearest pole: analyticity gives convergence inside that disc, while convergence across a genuine pole is impossible. Apply the coefficient comparison; no cancellation can remove a nearer pole under the positivity assumptions.
acceptance: Eigenvalues ±i√q have power traces 0 at odd n and ±2q^(n/2) at even n, so even tensor squares have traces 0 or 4q^n.
1/(1−2t)·1/(1−t) has nearest pole modulus 1/2; each factor has radius at least 1/2.
Dropping positivity allows (1−t)/(1−t)=1, whose infinite radius exceeds the radius 1 of its second factor.

sources.match: Even tensor traces give nonnegative coefficients; coefficient comparison controls the radii and hence the poles of the local factors.

nodes.title: Semisimple isolated fixed points: the full fixed subscheme has a fixed cone with no extra points
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, X separated of finite type over k, and let a linear algebraic group G act on X. Let g∈G(k) be semisimple and x an isolated point of the support of Fix(g). Let Z be the open-and-closed Artin component of the full scheme equalizer Fix(g) supported at x, and N_Z(g) the induced map on the normal cone N_ZX. Then Fix(N_Z(g))=Z scheme-theoretically. The scalar-twisted cone maps have a finite bad set of parameters, avoiding 0 and 1, outside which their fixed subscheme is Z. Thus the graph (g,id) has no almost fixed points in the punctured tubular neighbourhood of Z and satisfies the proper-component hypothesis of the normal-cone trace theorem. In particular, for any constructible finite-Tor adic complex F with u:g*F→F, LT_x(u)=Tr(u_x). X need not be normal or smooth and g need not have finite order.
hypotheses: Z is the full scheme fixed component, including its nilpotents; replacing it by the reduced point is invalid. Étale sheaf coefficients have ℓ invertible in k and the rational adic/finite-Tor conventions of EDC.0/6.

The reduced Zariski closure D of the cyclic subgroup generated by g is diagonalizable, with a torus and a finite prime-to-characteristic component. Cyclic density means χ(g)≠1 for every nontrivial character χ of D. This follows from the semisimple-element and diagonalizable-group theory already planned in ReductiveGroups Layer 4.
proofSteps: Work at x, without choosing a D-invariant affine neighbourhood. The stabilizer of x contains every power of g and hence D. Put A=𝒪_(X,x), maximal ideal m, and let I=(g(a)−a:a∈A) be the full fixed ideal. Isolated support makes I m-primary. D preserves I because it commutes with g. Choose N with m^N⊆I². The algebraic D-action on the finite jet A/m^N induces a rational D-action on the finite algebra B=A/I² and its square-zero ideal J=I/I².

D acts trivially on Q=A/I: g acts trivially, and equality with the trivial action on this finite-dimensional quotient is a closed condition, so cyclic density implies triviality of all D. Decompose B into D-character spaces. Exact weight projection makes B₀→Q surjective and places every nontrivial B_χ in J. Since χ(g)−1 is a nonzero scalar for χ≠0, the images of (g−1)B generate J from these spaces.

For any coefficient b∈B, choose b₀∈B₀ with the same image in Q, and write b=b₀+j with j∈J. Multiplying a nontrivial-weight generator in J by j gives zero because J²=0; multiplication by b₀ preserves its nontrivial weight. Therefore J has no trivial-character component, and g−1 is invertible on J. This proves the essential conormal claim even though the original local algebra need not itself be a rational D-module.

The surjection Sym_Q(J)→gr_I(A) generates the cone algebra in degree one over degree-zero Q. In the fixed-scheme quotient, every generator of J_χ vanishes because its eigenvalue χ(g) is not 1. Hence that quotient is exactly Q, retaining its nilpotents. Only finitely many eigenvalues λ occur in J. Scalar parameter t replaces them by tλ, so the exceptional parameters are among λ⁻¹, a finite set omitting 0 and 1. The same statement includes the zero parameter by the cone contraction. Shrink X about x to remove other fixed components; local conormal calculations give the scheme assertion along Z.

Z is finite Artin and therefore proper. Apply EDC.8/normal-cone-trace-comparison, Varshavsky Theorem 4.10(b), to the graph along Z; it requires no extra fixed points in the punctured cone and properness of the component. The restricted graph is the identity on Z. Nilpotent invariance of the étale site identifies its compact trace with the alternating stalk trace at x. This yields the local-term equality. For proper X with finite fixed support, sum these equalities in Lefschetz–Verdier.
acceptance: For char(k)≠2, X=Spec k[x,y,z]/(x³+yz), g(x,y,z)=(x,−y,−z): Fix(g)=Spec k[x]/(x³), I=(y,z), and J has eigenvalue −1. The full fixed cone has fixed subscheme Z, so LT_0 is the stalk trace. The cone at the reduced origin still has the fixed x-line, demonstrating why that false comparison is unnecessary.

On the same singular X, let t∈k× have infinite order and let g(x,y,z)=(x,ty,t⁻¹z). The full fixed subscheme is again k[x]/(x³), and J has weights t,t⁻¹. The finite bad set is {t,t⁻¹}, avoiding 1: this checks the general infinite-order semisimple application.
For g(a)=λa on 𝔸¹ with λ≠1, the full fixed scheme is the origin and the only bad scalar is λ⁻¹. If X is itself a zero-dimensional Artin scheme and g=id, Z=X, J=0 and the punctured cone is empty.

In characteristic p, translation g(a)=a+1 on ℙ¹ is unipotent of order p and has one fixed point at ∞. Its local term on the constant sheaf is 2 whereas the stalk trace is 1. It fails the semisimplicity and nontrivial-conormal-weight hypotheses.

sources.match: Rational representations of a diagonalizable group split into character spaces with exact projection; this supplies the finite-jet and square-zero conormal argument above.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.10(b) and Lemma 5.1, p.995; Corollaries 5.4 and 5.6, p.996 (version of record)
sources.match: The trace comparison applies along the proper full fixed component. The local algebra proof above independently establishes its hypothesis; it does not use the false general fixed-cone comparison recorded in E703/E704.

gaps.title: Semisimplicity of the characteristic-zero decomposition over smaller coefficient fields
gaps.detail: BBD 6.2.5 is stated with ℂ (equivalently ℚ̄_ℓ) coefficients. For K defined over a subfield E ⊂ ℂ (for example ℚ) with K ⊗ ℂ semisimple of geometric origin, the vanishing of the degree-one connecting maps of the perverse truncation triangles descends to E because Hom spaces commute with coefficient extension, so Rf_*K ≅ ⊕ pH^i(Rf_*K)[−i] over E. Semisimplicity of the pH^i over E additionally needs Galois descent of subobjects of perverse sheaves along coefficient extension, which EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension (Hom ⊗ E′ compatibility) does not state. The node asserts the splitting over E and records semisimplicity over E as this gap.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 5.1, Corollaries 5.2 and 5.4, published §5 pp.995–997; preprint v3 pp.10–11
sourceIssues.printed: Claims that taking diagonalizable-group fixed schemes commutes with the normal cone and consequently that the fixed cone has no points outside a group-fixed vertex.
sourceIssues.correction: The general comparison is false. Require and prove suitable smooth hypotheses, or replace the cone step by an independent argument. For the full fixed subscheme of a tame finite-order automorphism, the review supplies a restricted true statement and an independent proof; this does not restore the claimed comparison for arbitrary invariant Z. For an isolated fixed point of a general semisimple element, the finite-jet proof along the full Artin fixed component establishes the needed cone hypothesis; it likewise proves no comparison for arbitrary invariant Z.
sourceIssues.reason: Take char k≠2, X=𝔸², g(u,v)=(−u,−v), Z=V(uv). This is a reduced invariant Cartier divisor and D=µ₂ is reduced. N_ZX=Spec k[u,v,t]/(uv), with g(t)=t, so (N_ZX)^D=Spec k[t]. But X^D=Z^D=Spec k and N_(Z^D)(X^D)=Spec k. The proof substitutes vector-space coinvariants for the algebra quotient by the ideal of differences defining fixed schemes.
searched: Primary journal article and correction search on 2026-10-13; atlas errata register

review.reason: Computed the invariant Cartier-divisor example: the normal cone has a fixed affine line, whereas the cone of the fixed pair is a point. The algebra fixed quotient is not vector-space coinvariants.

sourceIssues.locator: Corollary 5.6, published p.997; preprint v3 p.11, with its proof through Corollary 5.4
sourceIssues.printed: Claims that a semisimple group element at every isolated fixed point has no nonzero fixed points on the tangent cone.
sourceIssues.correction: The implication needs an additional hypothesis, for instance smoothness at the fixed point with the smooth fixed-locus tangent theorem. The local-term equality itself is not refuted by this example. The full Artin fixed-component argument in EDC.8/semisimple-isolated-fixed-subscheme-normal-cone proves the local-term equality independently, including the singular example.
sourceIssues.reason: Take char k≠2, X=Spec k[x,y,z]/(x³+yz), g=(x,−y,−z), lying in the torus of weights (0,1,−1). This tame involution has X^g=Spec k[x]/(x³), supported at the isolated origin. But N_0X=Spec k[x,y,z]/(yz), and its fixed scheme is Spec k[x], containing nonzero points.
searched: Primary journal article and correction search on 2026-10-13; atlas errata register

review.reason: Computed the singular torus example: the full fixed ring is k[x]/(x³), but the reduced-point tangent cone has fixed ring k[x]. This refutes the cone implication, not the independently repaired local-term equality.

Weil II 6.1.3: generic shrinking makes ordinary images mixed through Poincaré/compact-support comparison; this is a first step, not a global purity theorem.
Geometric versus arithmetic semisimplicity is distinguished through the actual Weil representation and monodromy closure; finite-index component handling is explicit.
Weil II 6.1.1 and 6.2.2: cohomology weights are shifted by degree. Corrected both fixed-ι API and statement references to the local sheaf-purity owner.
Weil II 3.4.10: potentially P includes an actual finite-type model and all closed-fibre witnesses; it is not a label that assumes arithmetic descent.
Weil II 6.2.6: properness combines opposite weight bounds. Corrected the j* curve-complex example to cite 6.2.5(c), p.248.
Weil II 6.2.2: lower weights use Verdier duality and purity is their intersection with upper weights; ordinary stalk weights alone do not define complex purity.
Weil II 6.1.11: the proof first establishes f! mixedness and then internal Hom/duality, avoiding a circular appeal to all six operations.
Weil II 6.2.5: Tate twists subtract 2r and shifts add r to complex weight; smooth lisse purity uses the dualizing [2d](d) normalization.
Weil I 3.3–3.6: even tensor traces give nonnegative local factors and finite-coefficient product comparison; no alternating-form hypothesis is added.

Verified the independent finite-jet proof along the full Artin fixed component: diagonalizable weight projection kills positive cone generators and yields the no-almost hypothesis for Theorem 4.10(b).
